tiers.why: Crushing Maw sustains close trades and Web Lash creates access; Consume rewards a team that can keep targets nearby.
tiers.watch: Jungle is his smaller-sample role, and 1.17 cut his magical scaling, so keep the durable health route. Interrupted Consume and repeated disengage still deny the plan.
tiers.reason: 1.17 cut magical-power scaling on Hellfire, Web Lash, Crushing Maw and Consume and raised Crushing Maw's bonus-health scaling 4% to 4.5%. The 2.32 jungle plan is a health route (Elafrost > Fist Of Razuul > Flux Matrix, Death From Above), so the job is intact. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 52.9% over 807; 1.17 Gold+ 49.1% over 57 [36.6, 61.7]; Bronze+ 43.1% over 116 (nested). Under 100 Gold+ games, so no grade move. Grade retained; watch rewritten to state the 1.17 scaling shift instead of only the role-size comparison.
tiers.limitation: 57 Gold+ games is below eligibility; the Bronze+ figure contains the same games. Magnitude of the magic-scaling cut on a health build is not measured.

tiers.why: Glacial Charge, its Glacial Thorns root crystals and Hoarfrost give repeatable access, control and escape; Cryoseism can punish enemies gathering around an objective.
tiers.watch: Jungle is the priority on current role evidence. Do not transfer that grade to offlane or support, and keep an exit after the first control cycle.
tiers.reason: Only 1.17 change is Shatter's on-hit magical scaling 30% to 25%, minor for a control-first plan (Magnify > Elafrost > Gaia Greaves). 1.16.4 Gold+ review 54.1% over 3762; 1.17 Gold+ 56.1% over 314 [50.5, 61.4]; Bronze+ 54.9% over 681 (nested). S retained; why now names the plan's Glacial Thorns augment, whose dash-start crystals root.
tiers.limitation: 1.5 days of patch data; Bronze+ is not independent of Gold+.

tiers.why: Skull Crusher and Cursed Edge can set up a heavy-hit sequence, with Kingslayer converting a reachable catch.
tiers.watch: Current results and committed entry make this a comfort pick. Avoid relying on disputed Berserk scaling or assuming faster attacks solve his access problems.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 Bayle change. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 44.4% over 1495; 1.17 Gold+ 41.9% over 86 [32.0, 52.4]; Bronze+ 44.1% over 245 (nested). The Berserk passive text still carries the official-notes progression, so the disputed-scaling caution stands. Text agrees with the 2.32 plan (Berserker's Axe, Betrayer's Reqiuem).
tiers.limitation: 86 Gold+ games is below eligibility; no grade case either way.

tiers.why: Detection Protocol helps locate a route into a fight; Chrono Swipe and Primeval Roar support sustained contact after entry.
tiers.watch: Near-even results make this a dependable option rather than a statistical standout. Ursine Burst still needs allied follow-up and an exit plan.
tiers.reason: No Boris change; the plan's Wind-Rider attack speed fell 20% to 15%, a minor loss. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 51.9% over 3606; 1.17 Gold+ 53.0% over 270 [47.0, 58.8]; Bronze+ 51.9% over 621 (nested). Text still matches the 2.32 plan (scent trail, dash contact, canister window).
tiers.limitation: Interval is wide; the Wind-Rider cut is not separately measured.

tiers.why: Shadow Slip and Blade Siphon support short trades; the fixed Feast now gives a real targeted conversion after two abilities apply Haemorrhage.
tiers.watch: A practiced option: the jungle sample since the fix is small and her roles did not all move together. Mark a safe Shadow Slip return point before committing Feast.
tiers.reason: Official 1.17 bug fix raises Feast's delivered damage from 125/105/85 to 135/200/265 (rank 2 roughly doubled, rank 3 roughly tripled), and base attack speed rises 110 to 115. Feast is the conversion named in her job, so the 1.16.4 result was measured on a bugged ultimate. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 42.8% over 1059; 1.17 Gold+ 48.8% over 127 [40.3, 57.4], up 6.0 and consistent in direction; Bronze+ 50.5% over 303 (nested, so not independent agreement). This meets the brief's 'official change materially affecting the job, with 1.17 results consistent in direction' standard; one-step move C to B.
tiers.limitation: 127 games; the interval still includes the old 42.8% rate, so the grade rests mainly on the bug fix. Her other roles are mixed on 1.17: offlane 45.7% over 138 (down from 50.5%), midlane 50.5% over 198 (up from 45.5%).

tiers.why: Re-Crunch rewards correct ability sequencing and Cross Crunch attack weaving; Forward Crunch can preserve access for a second rotation.
tiers.watch: The combo breakpoint and sustained contact matter. A Ground effect now interrupts empowered Forward Crunch, so a lost escape can leave him stranded.
tiers.reason: 1.17 bug fix: empowered Forward Crunch is now interrupted by Ground effects. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 50.1% over 2567; 1.17 Gold+ 47.9% over 169 [40.5, 55.4]; Bronze+ 52.4% over 370 (nested, and the opposite direction). No grade case. Watch replaces the offlane comparison with the patch-relevant interrupt.
tiers.limitation: Small 1.17 sample; Gold+ and nested Bronze+ disagree in direction.

tiers.why: Safeguard and Hamstring enable short ability-attack trades before Earth Shatter can finish a damaged target.
tiers.watch: The dated jungle result was weak and early 1.17 results do not yet justify a higher grade. Ground now stops Reaping Dash's teleport; do not use the finishing ultimate as a substitute for an opening catch.
tiers.reason: Only 1.17 change is a Reaping Dash Ground bug fix, a small nerf. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 45.3% over 3481; 1.17 Gold+ 49.8% over 277 [44.0, 55.7], which includes the old rate; Bronze+ 48.4% over 568 (nested). A rising result alongside a nerfing change is not kit and evidence pointing the same way, so C is retained. Watch no longer calls the jungle result 'current' and adds the Ground interaction.
tiers.limitation: The +4.5 point move could reflect the 2.32 plan change (Malady > Omen > The Perforator) or noise; neither is established by 1.5 days of data.

tiers.why: Make Way and Sacred Oath create sustained gank pressure; Stone Forged Soul can extend the time he occupies frontline space.
tiers.watch: The strong offlane sample does not transfer to jungle, and 1.17 lowered his health and armor growth, so buy real defense early. Personal survival is not allied peel; the draft still needs a reliable catch.
tiers.reason: 1.17: base health 690 to 680, armor growth 5.4 to 4.8; the 2.32 jungle plan now buys Giant's Ring before Basilisk. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 48.0% over 1712; 1.17 Gold+ 47.7% over 107 [38.5, 57.0]; Bronze+ 46.3% over 294 (nested). Small durability nerf with flat results: B retained. Why now says gank rather than lane pressure; watch states the durability change and the plan's response.
tiers.limitation: 107 games; the durability nerf's size on a jungle route is not measured.

tiers.why: Smash 'n Grab creates a reachable target and Double Pain rewards continued contact; Warlord's Challenge helps punish a committed melee fight.
tiers.watch: Offlane is the preferred role. Long-trade strength does not guarantee access to a ranged target; Ground effects now interrupt Stampede, and anti-heal or disengage can stop the plan.
tiers.reason: 1.17 bug fix: Stampede is now interrupted by Ground effects. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 50.4% over 2920; 1.17 Gold+ 50.7% over 302 [45.1, 56.3]; Bronze+ 49.2% over 579 (nested). Flat: B retained. Watch adds the Stampede interrupt; E added to the cited keys.
tiers.limitation: Ground sources depend on the enemy draft; effect on win rate not measurable yet.

tiers.why: Shadow Walk can create an unseen angle and Crippling Dagger helps maintain it before Guillotine finishes a damaged target.
tiers.watch: The weak dated result and fragile entry favor experienced players; the better early 1.17 sample has no kit change behind it. Vision, enemy peel and the escape route matter more than an attractive burst total.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 Kallari change. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 46.2% over 2625; 1.17 Gold+ 52.1% over 169 [44.6, 59.5], which includes the old rate; Bronze+ 50.0% over 336 (nested). No kit or patch reason and no interval exclusion, so C is retained despite the +5.9 move. Watch now separates the dated result from the early 1.17 one.
tiers.limitation: The 2.32 plan changed her items (Vanquisher, Spear Of Desolation); whether that explains the rise is unverified. Revisit on a larger sample.

tiers.why: Ambush and Unleash support a direct jungle pressure pattern, with Cull converting a caught target and Invigorate extending contact.
tiers.watch: The large jungle sample is useful; weaker offlane evidence is a separate result. Anti-heal and disengage can deny sustain, especially beyond allied range.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 Khaimera change (the Passive text differs only in how level values are listed). 1.16.4 Gold+ review 51.9% over 9061; 1.17 Gold+ 51.6% over 728 [48.0, 55.3]; Bronze+ 52.2% over 1777 (nested). The most stable large jungle sample on 1.17; A retained. Text matches the 2.32 plan (Jungle Invasion, Invigorate cleanse and heal).
tiers.limitation: No case for S without a kit reason; stability alone is not a promotion reason.

tiers.why: Judgement of the Heavens can tether a target for sword-centered follow-up; Light of the Heavens and Fury of the Heavens support repeated trades.
tiers.watch: Both dated role samples were below even and the early 1.17 jungle result is lower, so treat him as a practiced sword-placement option. The Grounded sword-pickup fix is a reliability change, not a reason to promote him.
tiers.reason: 1.17 change: a favorable bug fix letting Kwang pick up his sword while Grounded. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 48.9% over 2006; 1.17 Gold+ 42.6% over 195 [35.8, 49.6]. The upper bound sits just above 48.9%, so the interval does not exclude the review rate; Bronze+ 45.3% over 342 (nested). No kit, item or loadout change on 1.17 explains a decline (his plan items and Nihil are unchanged), so neither part of the drop standard is met. B retained; the old watch's 'favorable patch direction' line was stale and is replaced with an explicit caution.
tiers.limitation: Close call. If a larger Gold+ sample's interval excludes 48.9%, move to C at the next review.

tiers.why: Boulder Throw creates an accessible catch and King of the Jungle supports the jungle route; Behemoth can extend frontline pressure.
tiers.watch: The plan's Rock & Awe rewards long boulder throws, so land the catch from range before committing Pounce. Early 1.17 results dipped without a kit change; health does not guarantee uninterrupted target access.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 Rampage change and no 1.17 change to his plan items (Overlord, Rapture, Cursed Scroll, Aegis Of Agawar, Giant's Ring, Void Helm) or Krix loadout. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 51.5% over 4006; 1.17 Gold+ 46.8% over 237 [40.6, 53.2], which includes the old rate; Bronze+ 47.4% over 445 (nested). No kit reason and no exclusion: A retained. Watch rewritten because it named Tiny Titan and 'a durable augment', while the 2.32 plan uses Rock & Awe (Boulder Throw deals 0-100% more damage by distance thrown).
tiers.limitation: The -4.6 point move is unexplained by any patch change; 237 games over 1.5 days. Revisit if it persists.

tiers.why: Hook-dependent access and the dated weak Gold+ role result lower default jungle priority. His support catch remains a separate job; a landed hook can still enable excellent follow-up.
tiers.watch: The grade depends on landing the hook. Keep an exit and preserve peel after a miss; his support catch is a separate job, and its grade does not transfer to jungle.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 Riktor change. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 46.2% over 1453; 1.17 Gold+ 45.4% over 130 [37.1, 54.0]; Bronze+ 39.9% over 203 (nested). Text still true and consistent with the unchanged 2.32 plan. [2.34 consistency pass: aligned with the other role reviews and the 1.17 ability text.]
tiers.limitation: Small 1.17 sample.

tiers.why: A committed, resource-sensitive entry plus the weak dated Gold+ jungle reference makes this a practiced specialist choice. The stronger offlane reference does not transfer to jungle.
tiers.watch: The larger positive offlane sample supports that role first. Jungle is a different result; manage energy and avoid relying on the disputed Ashen Vow base value.
tiers.reason: 1.17 only fixed the in-place Blink during Swan Song, a reliability change. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 46.8% over 2384; 1.17 Gold+ 47.9% over 146 [40.0, 56.0]; Bronze+ 46.2% over 416 (nested). The 2.32 review still treats Ashen Vow's base-damage fields as disputed, so the watch caution stands.
tiers.limitation: Ashen Vow base damage remains unresolved.

tiers.why: Heaven's Fury and Heresy reward attack uptime after a catch; Crushing Descent gives Ascend a brief stun to open the entry.
tiers.watch: 1.17 cut her on-hit and Heresy burn scaling and the Wind-Rider attack speed her plan uses, and early results fell. Enter after key enemy control is spent; a visage reset must be earned.
tiers.reason: 1.17 raises The Nephilim's bonus physical scaling 70% to 75% but cuts its magical on-hit from 15% to 10% of total physical power, cuts Heresy's burn from 14/27/40 (+25% bonus physical) to 14/26/38 (+20%), and the plan's Wind-Rider attack speed falls 20% to 15%: a net cut to the attack-uptime job. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 53.3% over 6998; 1.17 Gold+ 47.2% over 489, 95% interval 42.9-51.7, which excludes 53.3%; Bronze+ 47.8% over 1073 (nested, so not independent confirmation). Kit reason plus an interval excluding the review rate meets the standard; one step to A. Two steps are not warranted: the Weald proc-trigger fix partly offsets the cuts, the data cover about 1.5 days, and her second-wave dive job is intact. Why now names the plan's Crushing Descent stun.
tiers.limitation: About 1.5 days of data; the interval's upper bound (51.7) is only 1.6 points under the review rate. Statz still lists her S+ on lagging 1.16 data. The size of each nerf is not separated from early-patch play patterns.

tiers.why: Siphon and Reaper of Souls support a scaling frontline; Subjugate can hold a target for allies as durability develops.
tiers.watch: Protect the early soul-stacking route; both dated role results were slightly below even, so this is a practiced pick. Colossal Blow must not knock the target away from allied damage.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 Sevarog change. The old watch said offlane results were weaker than the smaller jungle sample, but the 1.16.4 Gold+ reviews are jungle 47.7% over 818 and offlane 48.1% over 2362, so that sentence was inaccurate and is replaced. 1.17 Gold+ 50.9% over 55 [38.1, 63.6]; Bronze+ 51.0% over 145 (nested). Under 100 Gold+ games: B retained.
tiers.limitation: 55 Gold+ games is below eligibility.

tiers.why: Line Tempo and Circle Rhythm support repeated trades before All-Kill! converts accumulated pressure; Rushing Beat helps choose the exit.
tiers.watch: Offlane is the more established option. She is a damage threat rather than the default damage sponge, and the jungle sample is relatively small.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 Shinbi change. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 49.9% over 637; 1.17 Gold+ 53.4% over 58 [40.8, 65.7]; Bronze+ 54.7% over 128 (nested). Under 100 Gold+ games: no grade move. Text still true and consistent with the 2.32 plan.
tiers.limitation: 58 Gold+ games is below eligibility.

tiers.why: Shield Bash and Shield Slam provide clear catch conversion, while Force Shield can protect an approach or the backline.
tiers.watch: Jungle rests on a much smaller sample than support, and the early 1.17 jungle sample is too small to judge. Heavy Metal attacks no longer break spell shields, so bring a real answer before engaging.
tiers.reason: 1.17 states that Heavy Metal basic attacks do not destroy spell shields; the jungle plan uses Heavy Metal. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 52.6% over 739; 1.17 Gold+ 48.4% over 62 [36.4, 60.6]; Bronze+ 48.5% over 101 (nested). Under 100 Gold+ games: A retained. The old watch's 'best jungler from raw WR' line addressed a past debate; replaced with the spell-shield caution.
tiers.limitation: 62 Gold+ games is below eligibility.

tiers.why: Ruthless Assault and Highland Hurl can pressure a held target; Unstoppable Force helps a committed frontline sequence.
tiers.watch: Dated results in both roles were weak and 1.17 made no Terra changes. The small jungle sample is not a default recommendation; use her as a practiced control answer.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 Terra change. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 44.6% over 543; 1.17 Gold+ 50.0% over 36 [34.5, 65.5]; Bronze+ 50.0% over 54 (nested). Under 100 games: C retained. The old watch referred to 'the patch's favorable direction', which described an earlier patch's buffs; rewritten.
tiers.limitation: 36 Gold+ games is far below eligibility.

tiers.why: Cyclebreaker/High Impact and stance mobility support repeated pressure; 84000 Hairs can create an additional threat after a favorable entry.
tiers.watch: 1.17 traded some health and armor for attack speed and cleave, so do not treat his damage plan as sole frontline coverage. The jungle sample is smaller than established staples; do not assume clones copy item on-hit effects.
tiers.reason: 1.17: health 680 to 665, physical and magical armor down 2, attack speed 110 to 115, basic cleave 15% to 20%, Windsurge base damage down with scaling 90% to 100%, High Impact minion damage down, clone kill gold up. The reviewed patch note reads this as a jungle gain and an offlane loss. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 50.8% over 1324; 1.17 Gold+ 47.7% over 107 [38.5, 57.0], which includes the old rate; Bronze+ 41.6% over 202 (nested). Mixed kit direction and no exclusion: A retained. Watch now states the durability trade.
tiers.limitation: Both 1.17 figures lean down, but Bronze+ contains the Gold+ games and Gold+ is only 107 games. Revisit if a larger Gold+ sample stays below even.

tiers.why: Windburn's extended attacks reward reliable attack time after a mid or support catch, and Backlash and Quelling Gale protect that window from projectiles. She still needs a separate initiator.
tiers.watch: A Ground effect now interrupts Lash Kick, so keep another exit. Reflection timing and target access decide whether her projectile tools matter.
tiers.reason: 1.17 bug fix: Lash Kick is now interrupted by Ground effects. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 52.1% over 2055; 1.17 Gold+ 54.0% over 213 [47.3, 60.6]; Bronze+ 52.7% over 444 (nested). A retained. The old why referred to 'reconsidering the old B priority', a stale review note; rewritten to describe her job, and the watch adds the Lash Kick interrupt.
tiers.limitation: Interval is wide; the Ground interaction depends on the enemy draft.

tiers.why: Severance and Soulstorm can convert marked targets into an extended sequence, with Hallowed Strikes rewarding attacks between casts.
tiers.watch: Near-even results support a practiced option. Resets need a Soul Rip target, and a Ground effect now interrupts Soulstorm; preserve a marked route that can also serve as an exit.
tiers.reason: 1.17 bug fix: Soulstorm is now interrupted by Ground effects. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 50.5% over 2067; 1.17 Gold+ 52.9% over 155 [45.1, 60.6]; Bronze+ 49.2% over 317 (nested, opposite direction). B retained; watch adds the Soulstorm interrupt and names the Soul Rip reset condition.
tiers.limitation: Gold+ and nested Bronze+ disagree in direction; small sample.

tiers.why: Barricade and Coliseum offer a clear catch for midlane or support follow-up; Evade helps him remain active through the next exchange.
tiers.watch: The stronger jungle result and easy-to-coordinate containment support this priority. Offlane is weaker, and Coliseum still needs an ally close enough to exploit it.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 Zarus change. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 51.6% over 5653; 1.17 Gold+ 53.3% over 463 [48.8, 57.9]; Bronze+ 53.3% over 698 (nested). Text matches the 2.32 plan (Flow State resets Evade on takedown; Coliseum placed where allies contribute). S retained.
tiers.limitation: 1.5 days of data; Bronze+ is not independent.

heroes.pick_when: Pick sustained contact and information when allies can convert his entry.
heroes.counterplay: Preserve displacement for the arrival, then break contact instead of feeding repeated attacks. Being detected changes the flank; abandon the ambush and reposition.
heroes.reason: All cited abilities are unchanged on 1.17. Detection Protocol still marks a nearby hero and grants trail speed; 'feeding repeated attacks' refers to canister attack speed and healing, so Passive is added to the cited keys. Consistent with the 2.32 plan's canister-window focus.
heroes.limitation: The Wind-Rider cut slightly lowers his attack speed after dashes; not stated in the note because the text makes no numeric claim.

heroes.pick_when: Pick a vision-led flank onto an exposed, damaged target after enemy peel is occupied.
heroes.counterplay: Keep vulnerable allies covered, track the disappearing flank and save control for the reveal. Deny isolated finishing opportunities rather than chasing invisibility through unwarded terrain.
heroes.reason: No 1.17 Kallari change; Shadow Walk still reveals her to nearby heroes and wards, Guillotine still scales with missing health and Death Mark reveals targets. The 2.32 plan's Vanquisher execute and Spear Of Desolation fit a damaged-target finisher.

heroes.pick_when: Pick a durable jungle catch that can land Boulder Throw from range, keeping Pounce for follow-up, peel or an exit.
heroes.counterplay: Watch the carried boulder, which Behemoth throws instantly, and spread so a Pounce landing cannot shatter it across several allies. Apply anti-heal while damage can follow; don't chase his jungle regeneration route blindly.
heroes.reason: Kit unchanged on 1.17, but the old text was unclear and incomplete. 'The second movement option' did not name anything (Pounce is his only movement ability), and 'the rock wind-up' ignored that Behemoth throws the boulder instantly. The 1.17 text also states that Pounce while carrying the boulder shatters it on landing across the area. Pick_when now matches the 2.32 plan's Rock & Awe (more damage with distance thrown). Passive is cited for jungle regeneration; E dropped because the text no longer relies on Rumble.

heroes.pick_when: Pick a practiced offlane skirmisher with reachable follow-up, and treat Ashen Vow's disputed base damage conservatively.
heroes.counterplay: Force mobility and energy expenditure before the extended fight. Spread from the ultimate's conversion area and punish the exit instead of racing an uninterrupted ability sequence.
heroes.reason: Cited abilities unchanged on 1.17; the Swan Song in-place Blink fix improves reliability but does not change the counterplay. 'The disputed base value' was unclear to a player, so pick_when now names Ashen Vow's base damage, which the 2.32 review still excludes as disputed. Counterplay retained.
heroes.limitation: Ashen Vow base-damage fields remain disputed.

heroes.pick_when: Pick a second-wave diver after the first enemy control is committed, with a clear route to the next target.
heroes.counterplay: Save peel for her reappearance or landing and deny the first takedown. Protect low-health allies: the resulting visage can extend Heresy and shorten the next ability cycle.
heroes.reason: Heresy (R) changed on 1.17 (burn 14/26/38, +20% bonus physical), but the note makes no numeric claim, so the text remains true and the apply script will copy the new R text. Heaven's Fury reappearance, Ascend landing (now with the plan's brief Crushing Descent stun) and the visage's free Heresy plus 65% cooldown cut are unchanged. Consistent with the 2.32 plan.

heroes.pick_when: Pick scaling frontline when the team can protect the early stacking route.
heroes.counterplay: Contest his early soul farming without blindly invading. If Subjugate chains you, stay inside until the chain ends rather than walking out into its stun, and avoid lining up for Colossal Blow into hostile space.
heroes.reason: Kit unchanged on 1.17, but the old counterplay said to 'separate from the delayed control area'. The 1.17 Subjugate text chains targets to the center for 2s and stuns any chained target that leaves the zone, so walking out is the punished response. Rewritten to the correct response; the souls line now names what he farms.

heroes.pick_when: Pick repeated magical trades and a finishing stack sequence when another role can absorb the opening.
heroes.counterplay: Back out before she reaches maximum Track stacks for All-Kill!, and punish only after both Rushing Beat charges are spent. Avoid treating her as a tank simply because she remains in melee range.
heroes.reason: Kit unchanged on 1.17. The old text said to punish 'a spent Rushing Beat', but Rushing Beat has 2 charges, and the plan's Allegro lowers its cooldown, so one spent charge is not an opening. The stack sequence is now named as All-Kill!'s maximum Track requirement, as stated in the R text.

heroes.pick_when: Pick her as a practiced, matchup-specific frontline answer when her armor-scaled control fits the draft; she is not a default pick in either role.
heroes.counterplay: Respect the empowered control and ultimate window, then trade afterward. Keep distance from the charged or committed sequence rather than feeding her preferred sustained melee exchange.
heroes.reason: No 1.17 Terra change. The old pick_when said 'buffs alone do not make her a default top offlaner', which referred to an earlier patch's buffs and to offlane only; rewritten to a current, role-neutral statement. Her Wild Rush, Ruthless Assault and Highland Hurl scale with armor per the 1.17 text. Counterplay still true (empowered root, Unstoppable Force armor and tenacity window).

heroes.pick_when: Pick mobile pressure and repeated access while another hero supplies the dependable frontline.
heroes.counterplay: Keep the escape route covered and identify the real hero before committing scarce control. Do not infer clone on-hit behavior or spend all peel chasing an expendable copy.
heroes.reason: E changed on 1.17 only in High Impact's minion damage (60% to 70% less), which the note does not rely on. 1.17's health and armor cuts reinforce 'another hero supplies the dependable frontline'. Consistent with the 2.32 jungle plan (Masterful Mimicry clones, stance mobility).
heroes.limitation: Clone on-hit behavior remains unverified, as the note already says.

heroes.pick_when: Pick a confident projectile-timing player into attacks her defensive tools can actually answer.
heroes.counterplay: Bait Backlash or wait out the projectile-control window, then commit from another angle. Do not assume a projectile answer stops ground areas or non-projectile control; a Ground effect now interrupts Lash Kick.
heroes.reason: 1.17 bug fix: Lash Kick is correctly interrupted when Yin is hit by a Ground effect. That is a concrete counterplay for her pull-and-leap, so it is added. Q is now cited. The rest remains true to the unchanged ability text.
heroes.limitation: Which heroes apply Ground depends on the draft; the note does not list them.

heroes.pick_when: Pick marked-target mobility and attack weaving after an ally creates the opening.
heroes.counterplay: Avoid leaving a chain of marked reachable targets. Punish Severance without its reset condition, and hold control, including a Ground effect, for the 1.5s Soulstorm channel rather than following her through every reset.
heroes.reason: 1.17 bug fix: Soulstorm is correctly interrupted by a Ground effect. The counterplay already advised saving control for the wind-up; it now names the 1.5s channel stated in the R text and the Ground interaction.

heroes.pick_when: Pick jungle containment with mid/support conversion and a disciplined exit plan.
heroes.counterplay: Do not spend burst into Barricade's damage reduction; step away from its stunning swing. Keep an escape or peel response for Coliseum and attack the unsupported entry. The arena limits movement but does not silence or stun everyone inside; continue using valid defensive tools.
heroes.reason: No 1.17 Zarus change; existing text still true. Barricade (Q), already cited, reduces incoming damage by 75% for 1.5s and then swings to stun. The old counterplay never addressed it, so a first sentence is added. Pick_when retained and consistent with the 2.32 plan.
heroes.limitation: The Coliseum movement limit is not described in the 1.17 R text; it is retained from the previous review as established behavior.

counters.reason: Use an alternate angle to force Sparrow away from her protected firing line before she spends the full barrage.
counters.limit: Her support may stop the entry; preserve an exit and do not count delayed Cryoseism as an immediate stun.
counters.review: Aurora's only 1.17 change is basic on-hit scaling; Glacial Charge, Hoarfrost's root ring and Cryoseism's 1.5s-delayed stun are unchanged, as are Sparrow's stealth reposition and 3.5s barrage. The tactic and limit still hold. The Pred.gg jungle table has no Sparrow row of 15 or more games, so there is no matchup signal either way.

counters.reason: Threaten the rock from an unseen angle and commit the leap only when allies can convert.
counters.limit: A missed boulder or protected carry turns the tank into free attack uptime.
counters.review: Neither kit changed on 1.17. Boulder Throw still stuns 1.2-1.4s and the 2.32 plan's Rock & Awe rewards long throws, which supports threatening from range. Pounce launches heroes backwards, so committing it only when allies can follow remains correct. Sparrow's stealth and barrage still punish a miss. No Sparrow matchup row of 15 or more games.

counters.reason: Enter from another angle after defensive displacement is spent and force him to move away from his area setup.
counters.limit: Do not chase through the full orbital field or assume your delayed ultimate controls him immediately.
counters.review: Legion's only 1.17 change is a larger basic-attack hitbox. Rally Point's knockback with brief Unstoppable, the Cluster Mine setup and the tracking Orbital Sanction are unchanged, as is Aurora's delayed Cryoseism. The tactic and limit still hold. No Legion matchup row of 15 or more games in the jungle table.

adaptations.when: Reliable attack access and a need for more basic-ability cycling
adaptations.reason: Trade chain-clear pressure for the item’s attack-triggered cooldown support. Respect the listed trigger limits; neither this choice nor a community guide proves an infinite reset loop.
adaptations.review: Storm Breaker is still in the 2.32 jungle plan (Sky Splitter > Storm Breaker > Draconum || Demolisher > Salvation > Legacy). Ashbringer is a completed item, unchanged on 1.17: 8% non-ultimate cooldown cut on hit, 4% against non-heroes, once per ability, 1.5x on crits. Storm Breaker's chained bolt is the clear pressure given up. 1.17's cut to Serath's magical on-hit slightly lowers the value of Storm Breaker's on-hit bolt, so the swap is no weaker. Text still true.

adaptations.when: Hero health and extended fights matter more than a later jungle-only clear benefit
adaptations.reason: A late swap for extra health and health-based magical damage in extended hero fights. Do not sell the opener automatically; repeated spells refresh the burn rather than adding independent stacks.
adaptations.review: Spirit Of Amir is still the plan's opener, and Megacosm is a completed item unchanged on 1.17 (health 250, Disintegrate 2.5% max-health burn that refreshes on reapplication, Star Killer 6% bonus-health damage). The swap still makes sense. The old reason said the item 'restores health-based hero pressure', which a player could read as healing, so it was reworded to state the actual gain.

adaptations.when: You can keep landing spells and nearby allies benefit from magical-armor reduction
adaptations.reason: Choose repeated-contact shred, haste and omnivamp over World Breaker's larger health-to-power payoff and tenacity. Neither effect amplifies planted-blade true damage.
adaptations.review: World Breaker is still in the 2.32 jungle plan's finish, and neither item changed on 1.17. Magnify gives 15 haste, 10% omnivamp and a stacking 6% magical-armor shred. World Breaker gives 350 health, magical power from health, a ramping magical-damage buff and 75% tenacity. The old reason omitted the tenacity loss, which matters for a melee jungler who must stay on his sword; added. The true-damage caveat is still correct because armor shred and magical-damage amplification do not affect true damage.

adaptations.when: You can keep fighting but need a larger health margin
adaptations.reason: Trade the late power multiplier for health and ramping magical damage. This does not turn Shinbi into a primary initiator.
adaptations.review: Oblivion Crown is still the final item in the 2.32 jungle plan (Spirit Of Amir > Oathkeeper > Magnify || Caustica > Spellbreaker > Oblivion Crown). World Breaker is a completed item unchanged on 1.17 (350 health, health-scaled magical power, Fiend stacking magical-damage buff). Oblivion Crown's +25% magical power is the multiplier given up. Text still true.

adaptations.when: You can maintain close basic attacks and value health-based on-hit pressure
adaptations.reason: Rapture supplies health, attack speed and close-range, health-based on-hit damage; Double Pain explicitly applies on-hit twice. Trade away Mutilator's power, haste, higher omnivamp and ability-trigger pattern. Kiting still defeats the plan.
adaptations.review: Mutilator is still in the 2.32 jungle plan (Sky Splitter > Basilisk > Mutilator). Neither item changed on 1.17. The old reason listed omnivamp as a Rapture gain, but Rapture has 7% omnivamp against Mutilator's 12%, so the swap loses omnivamp. Reworded so omnivamp is on the cost side, and Rapture's Nearsight damage within 475 units is named as the gain.

adaptations.when: Allied protection gives uninterrupted attacks and physical burst is not the limiting threat
adaptations.reason: Add attack speed and Prism pressure at the cost of Draconum's physical power, physical armor, some haste and its healing support. Heaven's Fury applies on-hit at reduced effectiveness; do not multiply full procs by every strike.
adaptations.review: Draconum is still in the 2.32 jungle plan. Neither item changed on 1.17. The old reason said Spectra adds haste, but Spectra has 10 ability haste against Draconum's 15, and the swap also gives up Draconum's 45 physical power, which 1.17's higher basic-attack bonus-physical scaling (70% to 75%) makes slightly more valuable. Reworded to list the real costs. Heaven's Fury applies on-hit at 35% effectiveness per the 1.17 Q text, so the caveat stands.

notes_for_team_review: Serath jungle moves S to A. She is in the jungle pool (zarus, aurora, serath, steel, rampage) and in the 'Second-wave dive' and 'Protected second entry' compositions. Her mechanics are unchanged in kind (Crushing Descent landing stun, visage reset), so the compositions can stand, but no text should call her the top jungle priority on 1.17.

Khaimera jungle (A) has the largest and most stable 1.17 Gold+ jungle sample (51.6% over 728, 1.16.4 51.9% over 9061) but is not in the jungle pool; the pool reviewer may want to consider her alongside Serath and Rampage.

Rampage jungle (pool member, A retained) fell to 46.8% over 237 with no kit or plan-item change on 1.17; the interval includes the old rate. Keep him in the pool for now, but flag him for the next review.

Countess jungle moves C to B on the Feast bug fix (135/200/265 delivered, previously 125/105/85). That fix applies to every role, but her offlane result moved the opposite way (45.7% over 138 vs 50.5% review) and midlane moved up (50.5% over 198 vs 45.5%). Offlane and midlane reviewers should judge their entries separately.
Wind-Rider attack speed fell 20% to 15% on 1.17. It affects every Weald (Dryad's Boon + Wind-Rider) plan: Serath jungle, Boris jungle and Sparrow carry.

1.17 Ground-effect bug fixes now interrupt Yin's Lash Kick, Yurei's Soulstorm, Grux's Stampede and Crunch's empowered Forward Crunch, and block Feng Mao's Reaping Dash teleport; Kwang can now pick up his sword while Grounded. Role notes or compositions that discuss Valmont's tether or other Ground sources should be consistent with this.
Kwang jungle is a close call: 42.6% over 195 [35.8, 49.6] against a 48.9% review rate, with no kit reason for a decline. Retained at B; move to C if a larger Gold+ sample excludes 48.9%.

Several shared tier texts in other roles repeat sentences corrected here. Sevarog offlane's watch says 'Offlane results are weaker than the smaller jungle sample', but the 1.16.4 samples are offlane 48.1% over 2362 and jungle 47.7% over 818. Yin offlane, Grux offlane, Crunch offlane, Kwang offlane and Countess offlane and midlane share the old jungle wording and should be checked by their role reviewers.

Steel jungle (pool member, A retained) has only 62 Gold+ games on 1.17. The 1.17 note that Heavy Metal basic attacks do not break spell shields applies to the steel/jungle compositions ('Direct catch, compact burst', 'Catch, silence, convert', 'Peel before damage', 'Controlled front-to-back').

tiers.why: Dread Nova opens a ranged damage window and Particle Shredder can keep pressure on a caught target.
tiers.watch: The midlane economy supports his damage engine; reposition before committing the beam channel. The early 1.17 sample has not shown a real decline, and 1.17 trimmed Lich in this plan's Vesh blessings.
tiers.reason: Grade retained; watch text updated. No 1.17 Argus change. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 50.7% over 4452; 1.17 Gold+ midlane 48.4% over 314 [95% 42.9-53.9], which includes the review rate; Bronze+ 48.6% over 644 contains those Gold+ games and adds little. The only related change is Lich (magical lifesteal 5/8/12/16% to 4/7/10/14%), which the 2.32 plan keeps with Tithe of Death as the stated alternative. The old watch leaned on much weaker support results (44.0% on 1.16.4); on 1.17 support is 47.9% over 146, so that comparison is a stale 1.16.4 fact and was replaced with midlane conditions. Statz A agrees.
tiers.limitation: 314 games over about 1.5 days (interval about +/-5.5 points). The Lich trim's effect on this plan is not measured separately.

tiers.why: Shadow Slip and Blade Siphon support short trades; Feast converts a target after two ability hits apply Haemorrhage.
tiers.watch: 1.17 restored Feast's intended damage, but midlane still asks a melee hero to trade into ranged lanes. Keep a safe Shadow Slip return and follow the jungler's catch rather than entering first.
tiers.reason: Grade retained; watch text updated. Kit reason exists: Feast bug fix (125/105/85 to 135/200/265) and attack speed 110 to 115. Midlane 1.17 Gold+ 50.5% over 198 [95% 43.6-57.4] includes the 45.5% over 2135 review rate; Bronze+ 47.5% over 406 is nested. Other roles do not point one way: offlane (her A role) is 45.7% over 138 and jungle 48.8% over 127, and the reviewed 1.17 hero note states the outcome magnitude is unknown. The fix raises Feast's payoff but does not solve the midlane problem of a melee hero in a ranged lane, so I retain C. The old watch ('Offlane has the useful current signal') was a 1.16.4 cross-role comparison and was replaced. [2.34 consistency pass: aligned with the other role reviews and the 1.17 ability text.]
tiers.limitation: 198 games; the interval reaches 57.4, so a C to B case may appear with a larger sample. Cross-role 1.17 samples are 127-198 games each.

tiers.why: Sticky Mine pressures a position and Tesla Dome punishes enemies held in a choke; Security Gate provides an escape or peel route.
tiers.watch: Midlane supplies the farming economy. 1.17 raised empowered mine damage and allied gate speed but made Security Gate cost more mana, so keep the gate for the exit or a diver rather than spending it freely.
tiers.reason: Grade retained; watch text updated for 1.17. Buffs: empowered Sticky Mine 110/150/190/230/270 to 110/155/200/245/290; Security Gate allied movement 40% to 50%, mana cost 65 to 75. Evidence is consistent in direction but small: 1.17 Gold+ 51.0% over 429 [95% 46.3-55.8] against the 49.5% over 5301 review rate; Bronze+ 49.1% over 804 is nested and not higher. A modest buff with an interval that includes the review rate does not support a move to S; A (strong alternative with a clear condition: a prepared zone) still fits. The 2.32 plan (Auto-Lock Amp, Azure Core opener) is consistent with the why. Statz A agrees.
tiers.limitation: 429 games. The empowered mine needs a safe basic attack; how often that lands in Gold+ is not measured.

tiers.why: Cosmic Rift supports lane pressure while Torn Space preserves positioning; Black Hole offers a clear conversion for jungle or support control.
tiers.watch: 1.17 trimmed Void Breach, Black Hole, Event Horizon and his mana scaling, so the grade rests on coordinated Black Hole conversion rather than raw damage. A Ground effect now stops Torn Space, and interrupts land once the Truesilver shield breaks.
tiers.reason: Grade retained; watch rewritten to name the 1.17 cuts. Nerfs: Cosmic Power 1% bonus max mana per 15 to per 20 magical power; Void Breach 100-260 to 90-250 and its cooldown scaling per 80 to per 100 max mana; Black Hole 520/780/1040 to 500/760/1020; Event Horizon (the plan's augment) 5% to 4% target max health; Torn Space now blocked by Ground (bug fix). That is a kit reason, but the evidence does not point the same way: 1.17 Gold+ 51.6% over 595 [95% 47.6-55.6] against the 51.2% over 9581 review rate; Bronze+ 51.3% over 1377 is nested. The 2.32 review kept the build, judging the cuts trim damage without changing its logic. A kit reason without supporting evidence does not meet the change standard, so S is retained. Statz still lists him at its top tier.
tiers.limitation: The cuts are small percentages whose effect may take longer than 1.5 days to show. Pooled matchup rows against Iggy & Scorch (39% over 36) and Howitzer (39% over 28) are too small to act on. If a larger 1.17 Gold+ sample falls clearly below the review rate, S to A is the first candidate.

tiers.why: R2000 Missile supports ranged pressure and Land Mine can protect an angle; Make It Rain follows a held target with an aimed barrage.
tiers.watch: Track the target throughout the ultimate. Movement during the barrage is not immunity, and a poorly aimed mine can spoil allied follow-up.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 Howitzer change. Review 51.2% over 2816; 1.17 Gold+ 56.2% over 203 [95% 49.3-62.8] includes the review rate; Bronze+ 53.2% over 372 is nested. With no kit reason and an interval that includes the review rate, the high early rate is not grounds for S. Text still matches the 2.32 plan (Combat Thrusters adds speed during Make It Rain; Land Mine kept for separating a diver). Statz B is a lagging comparison.
tiers.limitation: 203 games; the interval's lower bound sits just below the review rate.

tiers.why: Flame Turret and Oil Spill can control a lane approach and prepare objective space before the fight starts.
tiers.watch: Supply frontline from another slot and set the nest before objectives; rotations away from it are less comfortable. Inferno's turret attack-speed text is a 1.17 description correction, not a new buff.
tiers.reason: Grade retained; midlane watch rewritten. The only 1.17 item is the Inferno description correction (the turret attack-speed effect already existed). Review 50.5% over 3718; 1.17 Gold+ 55.2% over 239 [95% 48.9-61.4] includes the review rate; Bronze+ 56.2% over 603 is nested, so it is not independent confirmation. No kit reason, so B stays. The old watch opened with 'The strong offlane result', a 1.16.4 cross-role comparison, and was replaced with midlane conditions consistent with the 2.32 plan (Turret Maniac, Orb Of Growth). Statz A is a lagging comparison.
tiers.limitation: 239 games; Bronze+ agreement is nested. Matchup rows are 15-40 games.

tiers.why: Narcosis can create a catch for Hydroclasm and Brine; Genesis offers a further control and damage window.
tiers.watch: Current results favor a specialist pick. Bubble amplification timing, positioning and target access make nominal damage a poor guide to reliable output.
tiers.reason: Grade retained; watch wording corrected ('charged attacks' did not describe the kit; Hydroclasm amplifies after 1.1s and Cascade builds attack speed from ability hits). No official 1.17 Ikra change; the reviewed 1.17 note only records the Anomalies branch correction (no recall interruption), which the Vesh plan does not rely on. Review 46.5% over 2732; 1.17 Gold+ 46.8% over 171 [95% 39.5-54.3]; Bronze+ 44.2% over 346 is nested. Both agree with C.
tiers.limitation: 171 games.

tiers.why: Seismic Assault gives a compact catch into Void Bomb; Neural Disruptor adds a finishing threat that depends on the target's mana state.
tiers.watch: Midlane has the stronger role evidence. A missed Seismic Assault line leaves little catch, and maximum-rank Innovation effects should guide skill investment.
tiers.reason: Grade retained; watch updated. No 1.17 change. Review 52.5% over 6676; 1.17 Gold+ 52.6% over 536 [95% 48.4-56.8]; Bronze+ 51.3% over 979 is nested. The old watch said 'the attack-oriented augment requires a separate build interpretation'; both 2.32 plans now use Combat Veteran (passive experience and 3% movement speed), so that line was stale and was replaced with a kit condition from the plan.
tiers.limitation: 536 games.

tiers.why: A shorter Hive cooldown and Mark set up close-range pressure and healing trades before Curse finishes the marked target.
tiers.watch: Still situational: Curse does not solve entering Mark range safely, and rank-one Mark is slower on 1.17. Pick her into a reachable target with allied control; the early 1.17 rise is a small sample.
tiers.reason: C to B. Official 1.17 buffs aimed at her midlane job: Hive cooldown 14/13/12/11/10 to 12/11.25/10.5/9.75/9, Curse 300/430/560 to 320/450/580, health regen 1.3 to 1.5; Mark cooldown 8 to 8.5 at rank one but 5 to 4.5 at maximum rank. The 2.32 plan runs Cursed Infestation (Hive +12% damage, +10% range), so the Hive cut feeds the plan directly. 1.17 results are consistent in direction: Gold+ midlane 49.5% over 283 [95% 43.7-55.3] against the 45.9% over 2604 review rate; Bronze+ 47.4% over 530 is nested and only weakly agrees. This meets the 'material official change with 1.17 results consistent in direction' standard for a one-step move. B (situational or practiced) fits a hero who still needs an allied approach.
tiers.limitation: The interval includes the 45.9% review rate, so the move rests on the kit change more than on the rate; 283 games. Her offlane 61.0% over 100 is not a midlane signal. Statz C is a lagging 1.16 comparison.

tiers.why: L.I.N.X and Final Thread offer a deliberate spell sequence, with Data Burst supporting the next empowered tool.
tiers.watch: A practiced pick: correct sequencing and a saved Erase Vector are needed, and true and magical damage use different penetration. The early 1.17 rise has no kit change behind it.
tiers.reason: Grade retained; watch updated. The 1.17 Gold+ interval (55.6% over 223, 95% 49.0-62.0) excludes the 47.7% over 2854 review rate, but that is only half the standard: there is no 1.17 change to Neon, to RAM or Vesh, or to her core items (Combustion, Wraith Leggings, Amulet Of Chaos), so there is no kit explanation, and a high rate alone is not a reason to raise. Bronze+ 52.4% over 399 is nested, so it is not independent support. The 2.32 plan's switch from Ghost in the Machine to RAM changes our advice, not what players were doing (RAM was already the stronger observed loadout), so it cannot explain the rise either. A plausible alternative is early-patch selection: a practiced, lightly picked hero's first 223 games can over-represent experienced players; this is unverified. B ('practiced') describes her job. The old watch ('Current results are below the leading mids') was a 1.16.4 fact and was removed. Statz C.
tiers.limitation: 223 games over about 1.5 days. If the rate holds once the Gold+ sample is several times larger, re-check B to A with an explanation (matchup or item environment). Head-to-head rows are 15-34 games.

tiers.why: Soulfire and Stupor support wave pressure and catch conversion; Abyssal Rift gives a prepared team a sustained follow-up window.
tiers.watch: The current sample does not support an automatic top-tier claim. Protect farming and the channel, and avoid collecting Essence through an exposed route.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 Renna change. Review 50.1% over 6204; 1.17 Gold+ 47.7% over 405 [95% 42.8-52.5] includes the review rate; Bronze+ 47.2% over 932 is nested. A downward drift with no kit reason is not grounds for C. Text still matches the 2.32 plan (Netherward shield on Soulfire, safe channel before Abyssal Rift relocates her). Statz S is a lagging comparison and does not outweigh Gold+.
tiers.limitation: 405 games.

tiers.why: Harvest Nettles supports repeated lane pressure; Fly Trap and Bramble Patch turn constrained movement into a clear follow-up opportunity.
tiers.watch: Midlane has the larger established sample. Support is a smaller-sample option needing frontline elsewhere, and the delayed ultimate still needs setup or a constrained path.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 change. Review 51.9% over 7367; 1.17 Gold+ 52.1% over 532 [95% 47.8-56.3]; Bronze+ 53.1% over 1121 is nested. Text is consistent with the 2.32 plan (Wild Growth gives Bramble Patch 30% more range; Aion rewards steady Nettles poke). Statz S agrees.
tiers.limitation: 532 games.

tiers.why: Peekaboo! marks a target for repeated Knock, Knock! shots with attacks between casts; Back It Up! returns a target to where the team can follow.
tiers.watch: Carry has the better role result. The midlane plan stays physical with Sniper's Bounty, so missed shots cost both damage and gold; 1.17 trimmed Demonic Bargain and Satariel, which this plan uses.
tiers.reason: Grade retained; why and watch rewritten. No 1.17 Wraith kit change; 1.17 trimmed Demonic Bargain (350 gold at levels 1/7/13 to levels 1/10) and Satariel's major blessing (bonus stats 5% to 4%), both in the 2.32 midlane plan. Review 45.4% over 2820; 1.17 Gold+ 46.8% over 205 [95% 40.1-53.7]; Bronze+ 43.3% over 413 is nested. The old watch described Mystic Marksman's damage conversion, but the 2.32 midlane plan replaced it with physical Sniper's Bounty (Knock, Knock! killing blows pay gold), so it was rewritten. The old why credited Back It Up! with a repeated shot window; the repeat comes from Peekaboo!'s mark (75% cooldown cut on a marked hit).
tiers.limitation: 205 games; the Sniper's Bounty plan has no separate 1.17 Gold+ sample.

heroes.pick_when: Pick ranged catch and continuous magical follow-up when the team already has a durable entry.
heroes.counterplay: Move away from the crystal-supported firing angle and pressure from another direction. Bait Dread Nova before committing a dive; do not walk in a straight line through his firing lane.
heroes.reason: All four cited abilities are unchanged on 1.17. The text matches the 2.32 midlane and support plans (orb and crystal to constrain, safe Shredder contact, beam channel after repositioning).
heroes.limitation: None beyond the general small 1.17 sample.

heroes.pick_when: Pick prepared objective zones when the team can arrive first and hold an entrance.
heroes.counterplay: Avoid fighting in a prepared Tesla Dome. When a Sticky Mine attaches, leave her basic-attack range so she cannot empower it, and approach from a second angle to force a rotation away from her zone.
heroes.reason: Sticky Mine and Security Gate text changed on 1.17 (empowered mine 110/155/200/245/290; gate allied speed 50%, higher mana cost). The pick_when is still true. The counterplay now uses the 1.17 kit: an attached mine is empowered only when she lands a basic attack, and 1.17 raised that empowered damage, so leaving attack range is the direct answer. 'Spread the mine pressure' was vague and was replaced. Security Gate is no longer cited because the text does not rely on it.
heroes.limitation: How often Gold+ Gadgets land the empowering attack is not measured.

heroes.pick_when: Use a controlled entry into sustained area damage, with protection available for the channel.
heroes.counterplay: Save an interrupt for Black Hole and wait for any protective shield to break before relying on control. A Ground effect now stops Torn Space's teleport, so ground him to deny the entry or exit. Black Hole cannot be cancelled after 2.75s of channeling, so interrupt early and then leave the zone.
heroes.reason: Torn Space (bug fix: no teleport while Grounded) and Black Hole (damage 500/760/1020) changed on 1.17. The counterplay now adds the Ground interaction, which is a new, verified answer, and keeps the 2.75s transition, which is unchanged. The line about not spending every interrupt on the first frontline hero was dropped for length; the saved-interrupt advice covers it. No damage numbers are claimed. Cosmic Rift is no longer cited because the text does not rely on it. pick_when still matches the 2.32 plan (Truesilver protects the channel).
heroes.limitation: Which enemy heroes carry a Ground effect in a given draft is not listed here; Valmont's Arterial Grip is the midlane example.

heroes.pick_when: Choose ranged pressure with self-displacement and follow-up into an already held target.
heroes.counterplay: Approach around the mine angle and move throughout the barrage rather than standing under its aim. Punish his landing or spent displacement with a second engagement.
heroes.reason: All cited abilities unchanged on 1.17; text still matches the 2.32 plan (Land Mine displaces Howitzer too; Make It Rain homes on the painted target).
heroes.limitation: None beyond the general small 1.17 sample.

heroes.pick_when: Pick a practiced bubble sequence with allied setup and an explicitly chosen Eternal branch.
heroes.counterplay: Do not remain beside an amplifying bubble. Sidestep Narcosis and punish a missed sphere; check the actual Eternal before attributing healing or other branch effects to the enemy.
heroes.reason: All cited abilities unchanged on 1.17. The Eternal-branch caution remains correct, and the reviewed 1.17 note (Anomalies no longer interrupts recalls) does not contradict it.
heroes.limitation: None beyond the general small 1.17 sample.

heroes.pick_when: Pick compact, repeatable catch conversion when the team needs direct control from mid.
heroes.counterplay: Respect the Seismic Assault line and manage the exposed low-mana window. Remove or leave the drone's pressure area; do not confuse an empty mana bar with safety from her finisher.
heroes.reason: No 1.17 change; all cited text unchanged. Neural Disruptor still scales with missing mana (or missing health against manaless heroes), so the finisher warning holds. Consistent with the 2.32 plans.
heroes.limitation: None beyond the general small 1.17 sample.

heroes.pick_when: Pick short-range marked-target pressure when allies can supply the safe approach.
heroes.counterplay: Deny Mark range and force her to cross exposed space. Once marked and low, leave before the finishing window rather than assuming walking outside ordinary spell range removes the threat.
heroes.reason: Curse changed only in damage (320/450/580); the note states no number and its mechanics claims still hold (Curse targets the marked hero, Mark removed on cast). The Hive and Mark cooldown changes do not contradict the text. Consistent with the 2.32 plan's caution about acquiring the mark safely.
heroes.limitation: None beyond the general small 1.17 sample.

heroes.pick_when: Choose a practiced spell sequence and keep a reposition for the return trade.
heroes.counterplay: Avoid the returning construct as well as the outgoing hit. Track the empowered cast and punish a spent dash; magical armor does not negate the explicitly true-damage part of the return.
heroes.reason: No 1.17 change; all cited text unchanged. L.I.N.X still returns as true damage, and Erase Vector is the dash. Consistent with the 2.32 RAM plan.
heroes.limitation: None beyond the general small 1.17 sample.

heroes.pick_when: Choose farming and sustained magical follow-up into a protected, prepared fight.
heroes.counterplay: Contest the setup and keep a response for the ultimate rather than standing inside its full duration. Pressure an exposed collection route and punish a spent defensive tool.
heroes.reason: No 1.17 change; all cited text unchanged. Consistent with the 2.32 plan (Essence collection route, Netherward, safe Abyssal Rift channel).
heroes.limitation: None beyond the general small 1.17 sample.

heroes.pick_when: Pick prepared catch into magical area damage with a durable ally establishing the space.
heroes.counterplay: Keep movement for Fly Trap's delay, spread before the pull and avoid donating repeated Nettles hits. Approach from a second angle instead of stacking inside the prepared damage area.
heroes.reason: No 1.17 change; all cited text unchanged. Harvest Nettles still ramps on repeated hits and Fly Trap still pulls after a delay. Consistent with the 2.32 plans.
heroes.limitation: None beyond the general small 1.17 sample.

heroes.pick_when: Pick a practiced skill-shot carry with a clear damage-conversion plan and catch assistance.
heroes.counterplay: Use cover against the shot line and track the reveal and rewind setup. Check the augment before choosing armor: Mystic Marksman makes Knock, Knock! magical, while the midlane Sniper's Bounty build keeps it physical.
heroes.reason: Cited abilities unchanged on 1.17, but the 2.32 review split the augments: the midlane plan now uses physical Sniper's Bounty while carry and support use Mystic Marksman ('Knock, Knock! deals Magical Damage instead'). The counterplay now says which build does what, so armor advice is not misapplied to midlane Wraith. Surprise, Surprise! is no longer cited because the text does not rely on it.
heroes.limitation: Players may still run Mystic Marksman in midlane; the note tells opponents to check.

counters.reason: Hold Seismic Assault for the committed Feast or pressure the marked return point with allies.
counters.limit: A protection effect or missed line can deny the response, and 1.17's Feast damage fix makes a missed answer costlier; this is not proof of a winning lane matchup.
counters.review: Tactic still holds: Seismic Assault (1s stun, unchanged) answers a Countess who has leapt in with Feast, and Shadow Slip still leaves a Shadow she can swap back to within 3.5s. Feast's 1.17 bug fix restores 135/200/265 base damage, which raises the cost of missing the response, so the limit now says so. Pooled Gold+ midlane rows (Belica 59% over 17 against Countess; Countess 43% over 21 against Belica) are too small to weigh but do not contradict. The drone (E) is no longer cited because the tactic does not use it.

counters.reason: Use ranged zone pressure to contest the prepared space before the team commits inside the turret nest.
counters.limit: This is a composition-space answer, not a verified lane duel; Iggy & Scorch also plays midlane, and early 1.17 head-to-head games do not show Gadget winning that lane. Frontline still comes from another pick.
counters.review: Gadget's drone, mine and Tesla Dome are still area tools that can contest a prepared space from range, and the 1.17 mine buff does not change that. The old limit framed Iggy only as an offlaner; Iggy has a midlane tier entry and 239 Gold+ midlane games on 1.17, and the pooled Gold+ rows show Gadget at 38% over 26 against Iggy (Iggy 58% over 26 against Gadget). That is too small to remove the row but enough to stop implying a lane edge, so the limit was rewritten. Inferno is no longer cited (its text changed only by the description correction, and the tactic does not rely on it); Seek and Destroy is added as Gadget's main ranged zone tool.

adaptations.when: Little interrupt pressure and a safe allied entry
adaptations.reason: Advance the existing damage item and delay the bracelet; this reorders the same six, rather than adding a seventh item.
adaptations.review: The 2.32 Gideon plan still contains Truesilver Bracelet (third core item) and Wraith Leggings (second finish item), so the swap remains a reorder of the same six. Neither item changed on 1.17: Truesilver's Reprisal gives a shield on casting the ultimate with CC immunity while it holds, which is only needed when interrupts threaten the channel; Wraith Leggings gives 100 magical power, 11 magical penetration and Carnage (+12% ability damage against heroes below 40% health). Gideon's 1.17 damage cuts make advancing the damage item no less sensible when interrupts are absent.

notes_for_team_review: Valmont (new) has no midlane tier entry and none is added here. 1.17 Gold+ midlane 44.1% over 354 [95% 39.0-49.3]; Bronze+ 48.9% over 977 is nested. Hero-wide Gold+ bans are 9016 against 474 games, so his rate comes only from games where he was not banned. Pooled Gold+ rows favor most reviewed mids against him (Gadget 71% over 24, Ikra 65% over 17, Howitzer 62% over 16, Gideon 61% over 49, Iggy & Scorch 60% over 20), small but one-directional. Do not add him to the midlane pool on this evidence; give him a tier entry once a reviewed Gold+ sample exists. The 2.32 review records a source/official-text dispute on Bloodbound and Arterial Grip values, so counter or composition rows should not rely on those numbers.

Valmont's Arterial Grip Grounds its target. With the 1.17 Ground bug fixes this now stops Gideon's Torn Space (and, in other roles, Feng Mao's Reaping Dash, Grux's Stampede, Crunch's empowered Forward Crunch, Yin's Lash Kick, Yurei's Soulstorm; Kwang can now pick up his sword while Grounded). Composition and counter reviewers should account for Ground as a new answer to these movement tools.

Gideon compositions ('Containment into Black Hole', 'Protect the channel', 'Controlled front-to-back') still rest on a Black Hole mechanic that is unchanged apart from damage (500/760/1020); the 2.75s non-cancellable point and Truesilver protection still hold. 'Protect the channel' could add that a Ground effect now blocks Torn Space.

Morigesh midlane moved C to B on the 1.17 Hive/Curse buffs. Her offlane 1.17 Gold+ is 61.0% over 100 [95% 51.2-70.0], but she has no offlane tier or plan review here, and the reviewed 1.17 note warns against projecting the midlane improvement into offlane. Do not add her to an offlane pool from that sample alone.

Countess: midlane kept at C despite the Feast fix. The offlane reviewer should note that her A-graded offlane role is 45.7% over 138 on 1.17 Gold+ (review 50.5% over 1447), within its interval but moving the opposite way from midlane and jungle.

Iggy & Scorch shares the same why/watch text across offlane and midlane. I rewrote only the midlane watch (dropping 'The strong offlane result'); the offlane reviewer should keep the Inferno description-correction wording consistent.
Neon midlane is retained at B although its 1.17 Gold+ interval excludes the review rate; there is no kit reason. Flag it for the next review with a larger 1.17 sample.
Murdock's 1.17 buffs are carry buffs; his midlane 1.17 Gold+ sample is 10 games, so there is no midlane tier implication.

Lich (trimmed on 1.17) is in the Argus midlane plan's Vesh blessings and the Gadget support plan; the 2.32 build review already accounted for this and names Tithe of Death as the Argus alternative. Midlane pool (Lt. Belica, Gideon, The Fey, Argus) needs no change from this review.

tiers.why: Iron Rose lets her trade up close, and Imperial Lash or Queen's Garden opens the damage window; Crown of Thorns helps allies convert contact.
tiers.watch: Her dated offlane reference was weak and the early 1.17 sample is under 100 games. Tyrant of Thorns removes Royal Flourish's mesmerize, so the offlane damage plan is not the support peel plan.
tiers.reason: No official 1.17 change to Adele; all cited abilities are unchanged. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane review sample 44.3% over 1143; 1.17 Gold+ 52.5% over 99 [42.8, 62.1]; Bronze+ 52.4% over 206 (nested, contains the Gold+ games). The interval includes the old rate and the sample is under 100 games, so the grade stays C. Why/watch rewritten to describe the 2.32 offlane plan (Iron Rose trade, Imperial Lash or Queen's Garden damage window, Tyrant of Thorns) instead of a support-style catch, and to stop calling current results low.
tiers.limitation: 1.17 sample is under 100 games; the rise from 44.3% may be noise.

tiers.why: Crushing Maw sustains close trades and Web Lash creates access; Consume rewards a team that can keep targets nearby.
tiers.watch: 1.17 cut his magic scaling and raised Crushing Maw's health scaling, so keep the durable health build rather than a burst plan. Interrupted Consume and repeated disengage deny the plan.
tiers.reason: Official 1.17: Hellfire, Web Lash and Consume magic scaling reduced; Crushing Maw magic scaling 40% to 35% and bonus health scaling 4% to 4.5%. This favours the 2.32 offlane plan (Fire Blossom, Fist Of Razuul, Unbroken Will, Stonewall), which is health-built. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 52.3% over 2518; 1.17 Gold+ 52.6% over 171 [45.2, 60.0]; Bronze+ 52.1% over 286 (nested). No movement; A retained. Watch rewritten: the old jungle-size comparison is replaced by the 1.17 scaling note.
tiers.limitation: Early 1.17 sample; the net effect of the scaling swap on a health build is small and not separately measured.

tiers.why: Glacial Charge and Hoarfrost give repeatable access and escape; Cryoseism can punish enemies gathering around an objective.
tiers.watch: Jungle is the priority on current role evidence. Do not transfer that grade to offlane or support, and keep an exit after the first control cycle.
tiers.reason: Only 1.17 change is Shatter on-hit magic scaling 30% to 25%, minor for the offlane control plan. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 49.0% over 2532; 1.17 Gold+ 51.0% over 204 [44.2, 57.8]; Bronze+ 51.0% over 545 (nested). Jungle remains clearly ahead on 1.17 (Gold+ 56.1% over 314), so the watch text still holds. B retained.
tiers.limitation: Wide 1.17 interval.

tiers.why: Skull Crusher and Cursed Edge can set up a heavy-hit sequence, with Kingslayer converting a reachable catch.
tiers.watch: Current results and committed entry make this a comfort pick. Avoid relying on disputed Berserk scaling or assuming faster attacks solve his access problems.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 change. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 45.7% over 2135; 1.17 Gold+ 45.7% over 129 [37.4, 54.3]; Bronze+ 47.7% over 432 (nested). Consistent with C. Berserk attack speed is still stated only as an official-notes range, so the caution stays.
tiers.limitation: Berserk per-level scaling remains unverified.

tiers.why: Shadow Slip and Blade Siphon support short trades; Feast converts a target after two ability hits apply Haemorrhage.
tiers.watch: Early 1.17 offlane results sit below her 1.16.4 reference despite the Feast damage fix, so recheck as the sample grows. Mark a safe Shadow Slip return point and apply Haemorrhage before Feast.
tiers.reason: Official 1.17: base attack speed 110 to 115, and a Feast bug fix raising its live damage to 135/200/265. The kit moves up. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 50.5% over 1447; 1.17 Gold+ 45.7% over 138 [37.6, 54.0]; Bronze+ 46.9% over 292 (nested, so not independent agreement). The kit reason and early results point in opposite directions and the interval includes 50.5%, so no grade change is justified. The old watch ('offlane has the useful current signal') is stale on 1.17, where offlane is her lowest Gold+ role (midlane 50.5% over 198, jungle 48.8% over 127); rewritten. [2.34 consistency pass: aligned with the other role reviews and the 1.17 ability text.]
tiers.limitation: A at 50.5% is already generous; if a larger 1.17 sample confirms the drop, this is the first offlane A to revisit.

tiers.why: Re-Crunch rewards correct ability sequencing and Cross Crunch attack weaving; Forward Crunch can preserve access for a second rotation.
tiers.watch: The combo breakpoint and sustained contact matter. A Ground effect now interrupts empowered Forward Crunch, and a lost escape can leave him stranded.
tiers.reason: Official 1.17 bug fix: empowered Forward Crunch is interrupted by a Ground effect. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 48.3% over 3312; 1.17 Gold+ 47.8% over 232 [41.5, 54.3]; Bronze+ 47.1% over 435 (nested). B retained. Watch dropped 'offlane weaker than jungle' because 1.17 Gold+ jungle is level (47.9% over 169) and added the Ground interrupt.
tiers.limitation: Ground effects matter only against specific heroes (Valmont's tether in the patch context).

tiers.why: Safeguard and Hamstring enable short ability-attack trades before Earth Shatter can finish a damaged target.
tiers.watch: His offlane sample is small in both patches and favors specialists. Reaping Dash can no longer teleport while he is hit by a Ground effect, and the finishing ultimate is not an opening catch.
tiers.reason: Official 1.17 bug fix: Reaping Dash cannot teleport when hit by a Ground effect. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 45.6% over 406; 1.17 Gold+ 28.6% over 35 [16.3, 45.1]; Bronze+ 38.7% over 75 (nested). The 1.17 Gold+ sample is far too small to grade on, and C is already the lowest grade. Watch rewritten: 'weak current jungle results' is stale (1.17 Gold+ jungle 49.8% over 277), and the Ground fix is added.
tiers.limitation: 35 games; the very low rate is not evidence by itself.

tiers.why: Make Way and Sacred Oath create sustained lane pressure; Stone Forged Soul can extend the time he occupies frontline space.
tiers.watch: 1.17 lowered his base health and armor growth, so buy real defense on time. Personal survival is not allied peel; the draft still needs a reliable catch.
tiers.reason: Official 1.17: base health 690 to 680 and armour growth 5.4 to 4.8, a modest durability nerf. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 53.3% over 8824; 1.17 Gold+ 51.7% over 636 [47.9, 55.6]; Bronze+ 53.8% over 1495 (nested). The direction is slightly down but the interval includes 53.3%, he remains above 50% on the largest 1.17 offlane sample, and the nerf does not remove the lane-pressure job. S retained. Watch rewritten to carry the durability nerf and drop the jungle transfer note.
tiers.limitation: S is the most exposed grade to a cumulative nerf; a larger 1.17 sample below 50% would justify A.

tiers.why: Smash 'n Grab creates a reachable target and Double Pain rewards continued contact; Warlord's Challenge helps punish a committed melee fight.
tiers.watch: Offlane is the preferred role. A Ground effect now interrupts Stampede, and long-trade strength does not guarantee access to a ranged target; anti-heal and disengage can stop the plan.
tiers.reason: Official 1.17 bug fix: Stampede is interrupted by a Ground effect. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 50.5% over 5571; 1.17 Gold+ 48.7% over 509 [44.4, 53.1]; Bronze+ 48.9% over 1016 (nested). The interval includes the old rate and the fix only matters against Ground effects, so A retained. Watch now names the Ground interrupt; E added to keys.
tiers.limitation: Near-even in both patches; A is at its edge if 1.17 holds below 50%.

tiers.why: Flame Turret and Oil Spill can control a lane approach and prepare objective space before the fight starts.
tiers.watch: The strong offlane result needs composition context: pick ranged lane pressure when another slot supplies frontline. Rotations away from the prepared nest are less comfortable.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 balance change; Inferno's text now states the temporary turret attack-speed boost (a description correction). Cited Flame Turret and Oil Spill are unchanged. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 51.8% over 1921; 1.17 Gold+ 51.2% over 121 [42.4, 60.0]; Bronze+ 51.7% over 360 (nested). A retained.
tiers.limitation: Small 1.17 sample.

tiers.why: Ambush and Unleash give short trades once Lane Lurker builds Rage from minions; Cull converts a caught target and Invigorate extends contact.
tiers.watch: The large jungle result does not transfer, and the 1.17 offlane sample is small. Anti-heal and disengage can deny his sustain, especially beyond allied range.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 change (Passive text only reformatted). 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 47.1% over 766; 1.17 Gold+ 56.9% over 51 [43.3, 69.5]; Bronze+ 48.4% over 95 (nested, and lower than Gold+). Under 100 games, so no move. Why rewritten from a jungle-pressure description to the 2.32 offlane plan (Lane Lurker Rage from minions).
tiers.limitation: 51 games; Gold+ and Bronze+ disagree.

tiers.why: Judgement of the Heavens can tether a target for sword-centered follow-up; Light of the Heavens and Fury of the Heavens support repeated trades.
tiers.watch: Both dated role samples were below even and early 1.17 results are too, so treat him as a practiced sword-placement option for controlled fights. The Grounded sword-pickup fix is a reliability change, not a reason to promote him.
tiers.reason: Official 1.17 bug fix lets Kwang pick up his sword while Grounded; cited abilities unchanged. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 48.1% over 2780; 1.17 Gold+ 47.3% over 205 [40.6, 54.1]; Bronze+ 48.0% over 394 (nested). Watch remains accurate (both roles below even on 1.17 too: jungle 42.6% over 195). B retained. [2.34 consistency pass: aligned with the other role reviews and the 1.17 ability text.]
tiers.limitation: Wide 1.17 interval.

tiers.why: Riplash into Shock Therapy or Skewer creates a dangerous pick when allies are in range to follow.
tiers.watch: The grade depends on landing the hook. The dated offlane reference was weak and the early 1.17 sample does not justify a raise; keep an exit and preserve peel after a miss.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 change. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 47.4% over 1527; 1.17 Gold+ 50.6% over 162 [43.0, 58.2]; Bronze+ 50.2% over 247 (nested). The interval includes the old rate and a higher observed rate alone is not a reason to raise. Watch rewritten: 'current offlane results are particularly weak' is not true on the early 1.17 sample.
tiers.limitation: Early 1.17 sample.

tiers.why: Minueta and First Intent support repeated ability pressure; Swan Song can convert a reachable target while the team follows.
tiers.watch: Strong current offlane results support a serious alternative, but energy, exit execution and the unresolved Ashen Vow base field make this a more demanding default than Greystone.
tiers.reason: No official balance change; the patch context notes only the Swan Song in-place Blink fix (reliability). 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 52.2% over 5430; 1.17 Gold+ 54.7% over 362 [49.6, 59.8]; Bronze+ 51.2% over 854 (nested, lower). The interval includes the old rate and a high rate alone does not justify S. The 2.32 review still treats Ashen Vow base fields as disputed, so the watch stays.
tiers.limitation: Ashen Vow base-damage fields remain disputed.

tiers.why: Heaven's Fury and Heresy reward attack uptime after a catch; Ascend helps choose the entry and preserve a route through the fight.
tiers.watch: The dated jungle result does not transfer to her small, weak offlane sample, and 1.17 trimmed the attack-uptime damage both roles use. Enter after key enemy control is spent rather than leading into every interrupt.
tiers.reason: Official 1.17: basic-attack scaling moved from on-hit magic to physical, and Heresy burn scaling and damage fell. The attack-uptime description still holds. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 43.2% over 294; 1.17 Gold+ 37.5% over 24 [21.2, 57.3]; Bronze+ 40.4% over 99 (nested). Already C; sample far too small to move anything. [2.34 consistency pass: aligned with the other role reviews and the 1.17 ability text.]
tiers.limitation: 24 games.

tiers.why: Siphon and Reaper of Souls support a scaling frontline; Subjugate can hold a target for allies as durability develops.
tiers.watch: Protect the early stacking route; Souls need ability kills. Colossal Blow must not eject the target from allied damage.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 change. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 48.1% over 2362; 1.17 Gold+ 50.5% over 182 [43.4, 57.7]; Bronze+ 50.0% over 370 (nested). B retained. Removed 'offlane results are weaker than the smaller jungle sample': the 1.16.4 jungle reference was lower (47.7% over 818), and 1.17 jungle is 50.9% over 55.
tiers.limitation: Early 1.17 sample.

tiers.why: Line Tempo and Circle Rhythm support repeated trades before All-Kill! converts accumulated pressure; Rushing Beat helps choose the exit.
tiers.watch: Offlane is the more established option. She is a damage threat rather than the default damage sponge, and the jungle sample is relatively small.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 change. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 50.1% over 3744; 1.17 Gold+ 54.7% over 333 [49.3, 59.9]; Bronze+ 52.4% over 639 (nested). The interval includes the old rate; a higher observed rate alone does not justify S. A retained.
tiers.limitation: Early 1.17 sample.

tiers.why: Cybernetic Shell and Shield Bash let him hold the wave, then Shield Slam and Force Shield make him a team-catch and projectile-protection pick rather than a solo-lane threat.
tiers.watch: Support is his established role; offlane Steel brings utility more than lane pressure. On 1.17 Heavy Metal attacks do not remove spell shields.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 balance change; the official text now states Heavy Metal basics do not destroy spell shields. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 48.9% over 3333; 1.17 Gold+ 47.2% over 284 [41.5, 53.0]; Bronze+ 50.6% over 541 (nested). B retained. The old why described the review's reasoning instead of his job, and the watch discussed jungle; both rewritten for the offlane plan.
tiers.limitation: Early 1.17 sample.

tiers.why: Ruthless Assault and Highland Hurl can pressure a held target; Unstoppable Force helps a committed frontline sequence.
tiers.watch: Her offlane results stayed weak into 1.17. Keep her as a practiced answer to a specific draft, not a default.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 change. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 45.4% over 2309; 1.17 Gold+ 41.1% over 112 [32.4, 50.3]; Bronze+ 37.0% over 211 (nested). Already C. Watch rewritten because it referred to 1.16.4 buffs as the current patch.
tiers.limitation: Early 1.17 sample.

tiers.why: Windburn and repeated attacks create sustained pressure, while Backlash and Quelling Gale offer tools against projectile-based threats.
tiers.watch: The offlane sample is small in both patches. A Ground effect now interrupts Lash Kick; reflection timing and target access decide whether her projectile tools matter.
tiers.reason: Official 1.17 bug fix: Lash Kick is interrupted by a Ground effect. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 52.2% over 719; 1.17 Gold+ 60.0% over 40 [44.6, 73.7]; Bronze+ 52.0% over 102 (nested). Under 100 Gold+ games; no move. Watch now covers the Ground interrupt and drops the jungle remark.
tiers.limitation: 40 games; high rate is not a reason to raise.

tiers.why: Barricade and Coliseum offer a clear catch for midlane or support follow-up; Evade helps him remain active through the next exchange.
tiers.watch: Jungle is his priority role; offlane is weaker in both the dated and the early 1.17 samples. Coliseum still needs an ally close enough to exploit it.
tiers.reason: No 1.17 change. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 48.5% over 2510; 1.17 Gold+ 47.8% over 180 [40.6, 55.0]; Bronze+ 51.9% over 370 (nested). Jungle still ahead on 1.17 (Gold+ 53.3% over 463). B retained. [2.34 consistency pass: aligned with the other role reviews and the 1.17 ability text.]
tiers.limitation: Early 1.17 sample.

tiers.why: Refibrillator attacks with Bad Medicine and Ricochet give a ranged attack-and-spell lane with a stun, and Neural Regenesis can save a planned fight; another slot must supply frontline.
tiers.watch: The offlane sample is modest on 1.16.4 and very small on 1.17. 1.17 raised both attack speed and base attack time, so it is not a plain attack-speed buff, and the Infuse change mainly helps the support plan.
