tiers.reason: Official 1.17: attack speed 110% to 115% but BAT 1.4 to 1.5 (opposite directions), Infuse missing-health modifier 40% to 50%, Neural Regenesis cooldown 160/140/120 to 150/135/120. 1.16.4 Gold+ offlane 54.5% over 576; 1.17 Gold+ 62.5% over 32 [45.3, 77.1]; Bronze+ 49.4% over 83 (nested, much lower). Under 100 games; A retained. Why rewritten from review reasoning to the offlane job (2.32 plan: Refibrillator attacks between Bad Medicine and Ricochet); keys now match the text (Infuse is ally-targeted and not the offlane job).
tiers.limitation: Offlane sample small in both patches; the dated A rests on 576 games.

heroes.pick_when: Pick a durable close-range facilitator when allies can reach her root.
heroes.counterplay: Step outside Garden rather than accepting an extended close trade. Bait Iron Rose, then pressure after the defensive window; check the selected augment before assuming Flourish has mesmerize.
heroes.reason: All cited abilities (RMB, Q, E, R) are unchanged on 1.17. The augment caveat matches the 2.32 plans: offlane Tyrant of Thorns removes Royal Flourish's mesmerize; support Seeds of Dominion keeps it. Imperial Lash still roots, so pick_when holds for both roles.
heroes.limitation: None beyond small 1.17 samples.

heroes.pick_when: Use a prepared turret position to control waves or objectives; supply frontline in another role.
heroes.counterplay: Clear or draw the fight away from turrets before committing; melee basic attacks destroy them faster. Rotate around the nest, avoid clustered oil pressure, and leave turret range when Inferno starts because it briefly speeds up the turrets.
heroes.reason: Inferno's 1.17 text now states that turrets gain attack speed for 3s after Inferno (description correction), so R's cited text changed; counterplay now uses that. Flame Turret text states turrets take extra damage from melee basic attacks, added as a clearing tip. pick_when still fits both offlane and midlane plans.
heroes.limitation: The turret attack-speed boost is described as temporary; no on-hit item effects are inferred on turrets.

heroes.pick_when: Pick direct catch and projectile protection, with enough allied damage to convert the control.
heroes.counterplay: Spread against Shield Slam, bait Force Shield and change the attack angle. Punish Bull Rush used to enter after his control ends; don't place both damage heroes on the same landing point.
heroes.reason: Cited RMB, Q, E and R are unchanged on 1.17. The only 1.17 change (Heavy Metal basics do not destroy spell shields) does not contradict the note. pick_when fits support, jungle and offlane plans, all of which are catch-and-protect builds.
heroes.limitation: None.

heroes.pick_when: In support, choose protection for a planned committed fight with another slot initiating; in offlane, choose her ranged attack-and-spell pressure beside another frontline.
heroes.counterplay: Bait Neural Regenesis before the decisive focus, or change targets during protection; its cooldown is shorter at lower ranks on 1.17. Spread from the bouncing control and track the actual Infuse recipient instead of assuming every build heals allies equally.
heroes.reason: Infuse (RMB) text changed on 1.17 (missing-health bonus up to 50%); the note makes no numeric claim so it stays true. Official Neural Regenesis cooldown 160/140/120 to 150/135/120 added as a non-numeric note. pick_when was support-only; it now also covers the offlane damage plan (Refibrillator, Bad Medicine, Ricochet).
heroes.limitation: Offlane samples are small.

heroes.pick_when: Use his health-built sustain and Web Lash terrain entry to occupy space while a damage ally follows; 1.17 makes him less of a magic burst threat.
heroes.counterplay: Leave Consume's pull cone and save a control response for his commitment. Avoid feeding close-range bites or a low-health execution; apply compatible anti-heal before the sustain window.
heroes.reason: RMB, E and R changed on 1.17 (magic scaling down; Crushing Maw health scaling up). The counterplay remains true on the new text; 'keep distance' sharpened to leaving Consume's pull cone. pick_when now reflects the health-built jungle and offlane plans and the scaling shift; support stays experimental and is not named.
heroes.limitation: Net effect of the scaling swap is not measured.

heroes.pick_when: Pick her first in jungle to force a route through layered control with damage allies nearby; offlane and support use the same control at lower priority.
heroes.counterplay: Keep an escape for the delayed Cryoseism stun and spread before it resolves. The selected Glacial Thorns leaves rooting crystals where Glacial Charge starts, so do not follow her through that launch point or into an unscouted wall or narrow objective entrance.
heroes.reason: Q, E, R unchanged on 1.17. The old pick_when was jungle-only; it now covers all three roles in line with the tier grades (jungle S, offlane B, support B). All three 2.32 plans take Glacial Thorns, which leaves rooting crystals at the start of Glacial Charge, so counterplay now warns about the launch point.
heroes.limitation: Glacial Thorns behaviour is taken from the reviewed 2.32 plans, not the base ability text.

heroes.pick_when: Choose heavy-hit dueling into reachable opponents, with another teammate supplying dependable initiation.
heroes.counterplay: Trade outside his empowered heavy-hit window and punish the committed approach with range or peel. Do not base an all-in on the disputed numerical Berserk progression.
heroes.reason: No 1.17 change; cited abilities unchanged. Both jungle and offlane use the same heavy-hit plan (Berserker's Axe, Cursed Edge), so the note covers both roles.
heroes.limitation: Berserk scaling still unverified.

heroes.pick_when: Favor short, isolated trades that apply Haemorrhage before a protected Feast; offlane has the stronger 1.16.4 reference, but early 1.17 results do not yet separate her roles.
heroes.counterplay: Mark the Shadow Slip return position and keep a response for Feast, which hits harder after the 1.17 damage fix. Break contact before two ability hits apply Haemorrhage, and avoid gifting isolated Blade Siphon healing. Pressure after her return or force her to remain at an unsafe entry point.
heroes.reason: Feast (R) changed on 1.17: the bug fix raises live damage to 135/200/265, and Haemorrhaged targets take 50% bonus damage while she heals for the damage dealt. 'Offlane is the stronger current role' is stale: 1.17 Gold+ offlane 45.7% over 138, midlane 50.5% over 198, jungle 48.8% over 127. Passive added for the two-ability Haemorrhage condition.
heroes.limitation: Early 1.17 samples.

heroes.pick_when: Choose him for practiced ability-attack rotations and a team that can keep the fight in reach.
heroes.counterplay: Disengage after his first rotation instead of trading into the next empowered cast. A Ground effect now interrupts empowered Forward Crunch; punish it when spent offensively and avoid stacking where a repeated control sequence reaches both carries.
heroes.reason: Cited abilities unchanged in text, but the official 1.17 bug fix makes empowered Forward Crunch interruptible by Ground; counterplay adds it. pick_when fits both jungle and offlane (same plan).
heroes.limitation: Ground effects come from specific heroes only.

heroes.pick_when: Use an isolated finishing angle after teammates have created damage and information.
heroes.counterplay: Bait Safeguard's spell shield before using key control, and group enough to deny the isolated target. Punish Reaping Dash used to enter; on 1.17 a Ground effect stops its teleport. Cover the low-health ally and do not offer an easy execution reset after the first casualty.
heroes.reason: Cited abilities unchanged in text; official 1.17 bug fix stops Reaping Dash teleporting through Ground, added. Safeguard is a 1.5s spell shield (Q text), added as a bait tip. Earth Shatter's recast after a hero execute supports the reset warning. pick_when fits jungle and offlane.
heroes.limitation: Offlane sample very small (35 Gold+ games).

heroes.pick_when: Pick lane pressure and a second frontline body, while another hero provides hard initiation and carry peel.
heroes.counterplay: Kite the 2.5s Stone Forged Soul stasis, which heals him and slows anyone close, then switch pressure when the ultimate commits and return after the crash. Avoid spending every major cooldown into that heal window while his carries attack freely.
heroes.reason: Q, E, R unchanged. The 1.17 base health and armour growth nerf does not contradict the note; Stone Forged Soul still heals more at low health and crashes after 2.5s. Covers offlane (S) and jungle (B) equally. [2.34 consistency pass: aligned with the other role reviews and the 1.17 ability text.]
heroes.limitation: None.

heroes.pick_when: Pick sustained melee punishment into opponents your team can hold nearby.
heroes.counterplay: Avoid long trades that build Bloodlust and Double Pain healing. Save escape for the pull or dash; a Ground effect now interrupts Stampede. Apply compatible anti-heal when he is actually healing; range and disengage matter as much as damage.
heroes.reason: Cited abilities unchanged in text; official 1.17 bug fix makes Stampede interruptible by Ground, added. RMB added because the healing counterplay rests on Double Pain's stated health restore. Fits jungle and offlane (same Sky Splitter plan).
heroes.limitation: None.

heroes.pick_when: Use jungle pressure to force sustained contact while a lane ally supplies escape denial; offlane is a lower-priority lane option that builds Rage from minions.
heroes.counterplay: Hold disengage for Ambush, then separate him from the target before sustain stacks take over. Invigorate cleanses and grants brief crowd-control immunity, so land key control after he spends it; time anti-heal to contact and avoid fighting beyond allied peel.
heroes.reason: Cited RMB, Q, E, R unchanged; Passive text only reformatted and is no longer needed. pick_when now covers offlane (C, Lane Lurker plan). Invigorate's cleanse and 0.25s immunity are stated in the E text and added as timing advice.
heroes.limitation: Offlane samples small.

heroes.pick_when: Pick sword-centered containment when allies can follow the same location.
heroes.counterplay: Move away from the placed sword before committing; respect the tether boundary without treating it as a stun. Do not stack around the sword and grant both the damage and control sequence.
heroes.reason: Cited abilities unchanged. The 1.17 fix (sword pickup while Grounded) does not change the counterplay. Fits jungle and offlane.
heroes.limitation: None.

heroes.pick_when: Choose a practiced hook player with immediate allied conversion and another peel option after the catch.
heroes.counterplay: Keep units or terrain between you and the hook line, then punish a miss without entering silence range. Do not offer a second clumped target to Skewer while rescuing the first.
heroes.reason: No 1.17 change. Riplash still attaches to the first enemy hit, Shock Therapy silences, Skewer suppresses a cone. Fits support, jungle and offlane.
heroes.limitation: None.

adaptations.when: You can stay in close basic-attack range and need health and attack speed more than Mutilator's power and haste
adaptations.reason: Rapture adds health, attack speed and a close-range on-hit that scales with your health, and Double Pain applies on-hit effects twice. You give up Mutilator's power, haste, larger omnivamp and ability-triggered hits. Early 1.17 Rapture results were weak, so keep this a matchup swap; kiting still defeats it.
adaptations.review: Mutilator is still the third core item in the 2.32 offlane plan, and neither item changed on 1.17. Rapture's 1.17 data: 30% attack speed, 300 health, 7% omnivamp, Nearsight on-hit 20 (+2.5% health)(+15% physical power) within 475u. Mutilator has 45 power, 15 haste and 12% omnivamp, so the old reason implied an omnivamp gain that is actually a loss; corrected. 'Health-based on-hit' was ambiguous (Mutilator's hit scales with target health, Rapture's with Grux's own). The 2.32 review kept Mutilator because Rapture was weak in 1.17 Bronze+ (162 games, 43.2%), so the reason now says it is a matchup swap, not a default.

notes_for_team_review: Countess offlane: 1.17 Gold+ 45.7% over 138 is her weakest role on 1.17 (midlane 50.5% over 198), despite the Feast damage fix; A retained but it is the first offlane grade to revisit on a larger sample. The midlane/jungle reviewers may want to note the same.

Greystone offlane S retained after the health/armour-growth nerf (1.17 Gold+ 51.7% over 636); compositions 'Controlled front-to-back' and 'Prepared objective control' still fit, but his personal durability is lower without early defense.
Aurora's hero-wide note now warns about Glacial Thorns crystals at the Glacial Charge start point; jungle counter rows #4 and #15 were not reviewed here and are consistent with it.
Crunch, Feng Mao, Grux and Yin now have Ground-effect interrupts on 1.17 (Valmont); any composition or counter row that assumes their dash or pull reaches through a tether should be rechecked.
Feng Mao offlane 1.17 Gold+ 28.6% over 35 is too small to act on; he is not in the offlane pool, which is appropriate.
Akeron compositions ('Compact catch with protection', 'Protected second entry') rely on Consume and Web Lash, which lost magic scaling but keep their control; the health build is unaffected.

tiers.why: Gag Grenade can deny a response while Rad Rounds supplies a damage window; Shrapnel Cannon adds armor shred and escape utility.
tiers.watch: Keep a target in attack range. The airborne blast can displace enemies away from allies, and utility does not remove the need for a carry damage curve.
tiers.reason: No official 1.17 Drongo change. The 1.17 text still gives Gag Grenade its silence, Rad Rounds its attack-speed window with the cooldown beginning on activation, and Shrapnel Cannon its 30% physical armor shred plus the airborne launch and push-back, so why and watch remain accurate. The 2.32 plan (Lightning Hawk > Vanquisher > Imperator, Bring The Boom, Weald) was checked and retained. 1.16.4 Gold+ review sample 50.7% over 9600; 1.17 Gold+ 53.9% over 651 [50.1, 57.7], whose lower bound sits below the review rate, so the interval does not exclude it; Bronze+ 52.3% over 1293 is nested and contains those Gold+ games. S is already the top grade and nothing points down.
tiers.limitation: About 1.5 days of 1.17 data; the upward movement is inside the interval. Weald's Taproot was trimmed (8% to 7% bonus physical power), a small loadout change that does not affect the job.

tiers.why: Tachyon Lance/Axiom Strike and Zero Shift let Eden choose a trading pattern; in the Focal Lens plan, a Tachyon Lance hit shreds armor before the physical follow-through.
tiers.watch: Heat and stance execution are essential. Her passive turns attack speed into physical power rather than firing speed, and she still needs a response to dive.
tiers.reason: Grade retained: no official 1.17 Eden change. 1.16.4 Gold+ review sample 52.9% over 3596; 1.17 Gold+ 52.9% over 289 [47.2, 58.6]; Bronze+ 52.3% over 587 (nested). Text rewritten: the old why rested on 'strong current carry results', a 1.16.4 fact, and the 2.32 plan changed to Focal Lens with Lotus (Vanquisher > Solaris > Nuclear Rounds). Its definition says that hitting an enemy hero with Tachyon Lance shreds 25% physical armor for 4s. The 1.17 Passive description no longer says she 'attacks at a fixed rate'. It now says she converts attack speed into physical power, so the watch states the conversion and no longer asserts a fixed firing rate.
tiers.limitation: The Passive description was reworded with no official 1.17 note, and the new wording of the conversion ratio is ambiguous, so no number is claimed. 289 games in 1.17.

tiers.why: Assault Mode and Pulsefire provide a magical basic-attack threat; Energy Shield can preserve a firing window against an important spell.
tiers.watch: His results were below the leading carries on 1.16.4 and are lower still in the early 1.17 sample; treat him as a practiced pick. Buy penetration for the magical damage he actually deals, and do not count the shield as a general escape.
tiers.reason: Grade retained at B; only the watch text changed. The 1.17 carry sample (40.2% over 127 Gold+ games [32.0, 48.9]) is the steepest fall in the carry table from the 1.16.4 review sample (47.9% over 2142). It does not meet either route to a grade change. (1) Kit or patch reason: 1.17 made no change to GRIM.exe, and his kit text is identical. The only related changes are loadout trims: Satariel's bonus stats per stack went from 5% to 4%, and Demonic Bargain's gold moved from levels 1/7/13 to levels 1/10. The 2.32 plan uses both, but Skylar's plan uses the same pair, and they are small. The Lightning Hawk > Plasma Blade > Imperator core also matches what players already build, so the plan change does not explain the fall. (2) Evidence: the 95% interval's upper bound of 48.9 is above the 47.9 review rate, so the interval does not exclude it. 127 games is just past the 100-game eligibility line, and Bronze+ 45.1% over 326 is nested and contains those same 127 games, so it is not independent agreement. The hero-wide Gold+ figure (43.0% over 149) is mostly the same games. A move to C would therefore rest on one small sample alone, which the standard forbids. I rewrote the watch instead: its 'current results' clause stated a 1.16.4 fact, and it now warns about the weak early 1.17 sample.
tiers.limitation: The drop has no mechanical explanation. It may be noise, an early-patch player mix, or a real weakness the 127 games cannot separate. If a larger 1.17 Gold+ sample confirms an interval below the review rate, C would be justified. The Pred.gg matchup rows (for example 25% over 28 games against Sparrow) are too small to use.

tiers.why: Mercy and repeated attacks build Vengeance before Dusk; Shadow Glide offers a way to preserve space or follow a confirmed catch.
tiers.watch: 1.17 raised Mercy damage and Dusk now refunds mana on a kill, but that has not yet lifted her early results. Purge is an exposed commitment that still needs control or peel.
tiers.reason: Kit reason points up: base physical power went from 54 to 53, but growth rose from 3.5 to 3.7; Dusk refunds 35% mana when it kills any target (once per cast); Mercy base damage rose from 20/25/30/35/40 to 25/30/35/40/45. The evidence points the other way: 1.16.4 Gold+ review sample 48.6% over 5474; 1.17 Gold+ 45.1% over 412 [40.4, 50.0], an interval that still contains the review rate; Bronze+ 48.5% over 765 (nested). With the kit and the results pointing in opposite directions, neither a raise nor a drop meets the standard. Text refreshed: the 1.16.4 'current results' clause was replaced with the 1.17 changes stated modestly, in line with the reviewed patch note ('do not promise free repeated casts or a new win-rate tier'). The why now names Vengeance, which Mercy and attacks build and Dusk consumes. The 2.32 Solaris > Ashbringer > Imperator plan fits this cast-attack pattern.
tiers.limitation: The buffs are modest, and the refund needs a kill; 1.5 days of data cannot show their effect.

tiers.why: Saturation Charge and Orbital Sanction offer area pressure alongside ranged attacks; the Scorched Earth plan adds napalm zones where mines, Frag Order and the beam land.
tiers.watch: The ability-oriented plan converts an allied catch, and bonus attack speed becomes haste, not firing speed. 1.17 widened the rifle projectile, but his early 1.17 carry result sits below the review sample, so recheck this priority as data grows.
tiers.reason: Kit: 1.17 increased the K-75 Storm Rifle projectile hitbox radius by 10%. That helps hit consistency but does not change listed damage (the reviewed patch note says the same). 1.16.4 Gold+ review sample 52.6% over 6656; 1.17 Gold+ 48.6% over 529 [44.4, 52.8], whose upper bound is just above the review rate, so the interval does not exclude it; Bronze+ 51.2% over 1289 (nested). The kit change points slightly up and the early sample points down, so no grade change meets the standard. Text rewritten: the old why/watch cited 'the current carry sample' (a 1.16.4 fact), and the 2.32 plan replaced Press the Advantage with Scorched Earth. Per its definition, Frag Order and Saturation Charge mines create napalm zones when they explode, and Orbital Sanction creates one every 0.5s. The Passive text still converts 1% bonus attack speed into 0.75 ability haste.
tiers.limitation: The effect of the hitbox change on hit rate is unmeasured. The 1.17 point estimate is 4.0 points below the review rate, and the interval only barely contains it, which makes Legion the S carry most worth rechecking.

tiers.why: Static Trap and Buckshot can buy firing space, while Long Arm of the Law converts a distant catch without abandoning the lane.
tiers.watch: 1.17 raised Shots Fired, Buckshot and Long Arm of the Law damage, which supports a practiced or matchup pick but not a default damage priority. Save Buckshot and traps for the diver.
tiers.reason: Kit or patch reason: every one of the three 1.17 buffs strengthens the job in the why text. Buckshot damage rose from 60/85/110/135/160 to 60/90/120/150/180 (self-peel trades). Long Arm of the Law rose from 250/400/550 to 280/430/580, with bonus physical power scaling from 115% to 120% (converting a distant catch). Shots Fired total physical power scaling rose from 36/44/52/60% to 40/48/56/64% (sustained attacks). The evidence moves the same way: 1.16.4 Gold+ review sample 46.2% over 5224, 1.17 Gold+ 47.9% over 541 [43.7, 52.1], and Bronze+ 48.1% over 1106, which is nested and so adds little independent support. This matches the brief's first example (an official change that materially affects the job, with 1.17 results consistent in direction). It is a one-step move. B (situational or practiced) is also what the old C text already described ('a comfort or specific-matchup choice'). It puts him level with the other sub-50% carries (Kira, TwinBlast, Skylar) instead of below them. Statz also lists him at B (comparison only). He stays below A because his 1.17 rate is still under 50% and the interval contains the review rate. The 2.32 plan (Storm Breaker > Lightning Hawk > Demolisher, Justice's Reach) supports sustained attacks and is consistent with the text.
tiers.limitation: The +1.7-point rise sits well inside the interval, so the move rests on the buffs, not on the sample. The 1.17 Passive description still lists the old 36-60% scaling although the official notes give 40-64%, so no passive number is cited in the displayed text.

tiers.why: Hellfire Rounds and Obliterate reward a short damage window, making allied catches a natural way to convert his burst.
tiers.watch: Reckoning can remove a focus target from allied area damage. Coordinate isolation, and do not buy attack speed merely because it suits another carry.
tiers.reason: No official 1.17 Revenant change; his Hellfire Rounds, Obliterate and Reckoning text is unchanged. The 2.32 plan (Vanquisher > Imperator > Terminus, Hellfire Blast, Thraex) was retained and buys no attack-speed item, which matches the watch. 1.16.4 Gold+ review sample 51.7% over 7583; 1.17 Gold+ 54.2% over 570 [50.1, 58.3], an interval that contains the review rate; Bronze+ 52.0% over 1078 (nested). A high observed rate with no kit reason is not grounds to raise him to S.
tiers.limitation: Early 1.17 sample; the rise is inside the interval.

tiers.why: Air Assault can change the firing angle while Hypercharge provides a committed damage window.
tiers.watch: Her 1.16.4 and early 1.17 carry results sit below the leading options. Flight is not guaranteed safety; choose a peel partner, and remember the Satariel plan loses its takedown stacks on death.
tiers.reason: Grade retained: no official 1.17 Skylar change. 1.16.4 Gold+ review sample 47.8% over 3390; 1.17 Gold+ 45.6% over 287 [40.0, 51.4], an interval that contains the review rate; Bronze+ 47.0% over 643 (nested). The 2.32 plan moved to Satariel (Demonic Bargain + Broken Wings). 1.17 trimmed Satariel's bonus stats per stack from 5% to 4% and moved Demonic Bargain's gold to levels 1/10; both changes are small. Text refreshed: the 'current carry sample' clause was a 1.16.4 fact, and Satariel's definition says Fearless stacks are lost on death, a risk for a flight-dependent carry. Her very high hero-wide Gold+ ban count (5820) is not win evidence; the Statz S grade is comparison only.
tiers.limitation: Heavy banning keeps her 1.17 sample small (287 games).

tiers.why: Relentless and Heightened Senses reward safe repeated attacks; Inner Fire turns an allied control window into a sustained barrage.
tiers.watch: This priority assumes someone buys attack time. There is no dash to rescue an exposed path, and the initial control will not last for the entire barrage.
tiers.reason: No official 1.17 Sparrow change; her Relentless, Heightened Senses (stealth, movement speed and attack speed, no dash) and Inner Fire text is unchanged. The 2.32 plan (Storm Breaker > Sky Splitter > Demolisher, Sun Shards, Weald) was retained. 1.16.4 Gold+ review sample 52.0% over 11430; 1.17 Gold+ 49.6% over 772 [46.1, 53.1], an interval that contains the review rate; Bronze+ 50.6% over 1837 (nested). The one relevant 1.17 change is loadout-only: Wind-Rider's attack speed fell from 20% to 15%. That is a small trim to her Weald plan, not a change in her job.
tiers.limitation: Early sample; the dip is inside the interval. The effect of the Wind-Rider trim is unmeasured.

tiers.why: Vaporize and Vortex Grenade support ability-attack weaving; Rocket Dash lets him preserve a firing position or follow a confirmed catch.
tiers.watch: 1.17's larger basic-attack hitbox helps consistency, not listed damage, and his results remain below the carry priorities. Do not spend the dash forward while a diver is missing or channel Ventilate into an available interrupt.
tiers.reason: Kit: 1.17 increased the Lunari 4.0 projectile hitbox radius by 10%, with no change to listed damage. Evidence is flat: 1.16.4 Gold+ review sample 48.9% over 7005; 1.17 Gold+ 48.4% over 581 [44.3, 52.4]; Bronze+ 47.4% over 1136 (nested). There is no case for moving him. Text refreshed: the 'current results' clause was a 1.16.4 fact, and the watch now states what the hitbox change does. The 2.32 Solaris > Vanquisher > Tainted Rounds plan still weaves casts and attacks.
tiers.limitation: The effect of the hitbox change is unmeasured.

tiers.why: Peekaboo! marks a target so Knock, Knock! fires again sooner, with ranged attacks between casts; Back It Up! returns a target to where the team can follow.
tiers.watch: Mystic Marksman makes Knock, Knock! magical while his attacks and the grenade's hit stay physical, so penetration must fit both. Missed shots sharply reduce this plan's value.
tiers.reason: Grade retained: no official 1.17 Wraith change. 1.16.4 Gold+ review sample 48.7% over 1552; 1.17 Gold+ 54.8% over 126 [46.1, 63.2], an interval that contains the review rate; Bronze+ 50.5% over 208 (nested). A high rate on 126 games is not a reason to raise him. Text rewritten for the carry entry: the old watch, shared with the midlane entry, opened with a mid-versus-carry comparison ('Carry has the better current role result'). The carry plan retains Mystic Marksman (its definition: Knock, Knock! deals magical damage instead), with Mindrazor > Vanquisher > Envy and Caustica, so the watch now describes the mixed damage. [2.34 consistency pass: aligned with the other role reviews and the 1.17 ability text.]
tiers.limitation: Small 1.17 sample (126 games) with a wide interval.

heroes.pick_when: Pick a carry with a silence response and physical shred for coordinated focus.
heroes.counterplay: Force Gag Grenade before the real commitment and disengage from Rad Rounds until its attack window ends. Track the airborne ultimate escape rather than assuming a cornered Drongo cannot move.
heroes.reason: All three cited abilities are unchanged on 1.17. Gag Grenade silences, Rad Rounds gives a 4s attack-speed window whose cooldown begins on activation, and Shrapnel Cannon launches him away when used in the air, with brief CC immunity. Both sentences remain true and agree with the 2.32 plan.

heroes.pick_when: Choose a mechanically confident carry player who can manage heat and stance while another hero starts the fight.
heroes.counterplay: Attack during an unfavorable stance or after repositioning is spent. Track heat and range changes; do not chase into the melee conversion simply because the ranged exchange ended.
heroes.reason: LMB, Q and E are unchanged. The Passive description changed wording on 1.17: the 'attacks at a fixed rate' sentence became 'converts 1% Attack Speed into 60% increased Physical Power'. The heat and Overheat mechanics the note relies on are unchanged, so the note text stays and the Passive key is refreshed to the 1.17 text by the apply script.
heroes.limitation: The Passive rewording has no official 1.17 note; the note does not rely on the conversion wording.

heroes.pick_when: Pick magical basic-attack pressure when the rest of the damage plan is too physical.
heroes.counterplay: Bait Energy Shield with a lower-value spell before committing control. His magical attack pattern changes armor choices; do not assume physical armor answers the carry slot.
heroes.reason: RMB, Q, E and R are unchanged on 1.17. Energy Shield still blocks the next enemy ability, and the plan's System Restore makes a successful block restore health and movement speed, so baiting it matters even more. Basic attacks are magical through Pulsefire and Assault Mode. The note is still true and consistent with the 2.32 plan (Caustica for magical penetration).
heroes.limitation: The weak early 1.17 carry sample does not affect what the note says.

heroes.pick_when: Pick a follow-up carry when allies can buy a sustained firing or Purge window.
heroes.counterplay: Keep an interrupt for Purge and pressure after Shadow Glide is used. Break the extended attack exchange rather than allowing her to build stacks on an undefended frontline target.
heroes.reason: The cited E, R and Passive text is unchanged. The 1.17 changes (Mercy damage, the Dusk mana refund on a kill, the base power curve) do not contradict the note. Purge still stops her from attacking or casting anything except Shadow Glide, and it slows her by 30%, which supports 'keep an interrupt for Purge'. The note agrees with the 2.32 Solaris > Ashbringer plan.

heroes.pick_when: Pick physical area damage into an allied catch, with another slot protecting the backline.
heroes.counterplay: Leave Orbital Sanction's path and re-engage after the standard or defensive displacement is spent. Do not hold ground in his napalm: the Scorched Earth plan leaves burning zones where mines and Frag Order explode and under the beam.
heroes.reason: The old second sentence said the reviewed Press the Advantage plan removes Rally Point healing. The 2.32 plan replaced that augment with Scorched Earth, which does not remove the healing; per its definition, Frag Order and Saturation Charge mines create napalm zones and Orbital Sanction creates one every 0.5s. The first sentence is still true: Rally Point knocks back and makes him Unstoppable for 0.5s, and Frag Order can launch Legion. RMB was added because the counterplay now relies on Frag Order and on its self-launch. Passive was dropped because the note no longer relies on it.
heroes.limitation: The napalm zones' damage (5 plus 6% bonus physical power per 0.5s) is modest; the advice is not to stand in them, not that they are lethal.

heroes.pick_when: Choose self-peel and distant catch conversion for a practiced carry; 1.17 raised Buckshot and Long Arm of the Law damage but does not make him a default pick.
heroes.counterplay: Approach around armed traps, preserve movement after Buckshot and respect the distant shot when low. Force the escape before the main diver enters.
heroes.reason: The Buckshot (RMB) and Long Arm of the Law (R) text changed on 1.17 because their damage rose. The mechanics the note relies on (terrain-piercing blast with push-back and shred; unlimited-range shot) are unchanged. The old pick_when ended 'not for a high current role result', a 1.16.4 framing. It now states the 1.17 buff without promising a default pick, consistent with the grade moving from C to B. The counterplay is still true: Static Trap roots, Hot Pursuit is his movement escape and resets on takedown, and the sniper shot is unlimited range.
heroes.limitation: No numbers from the Passive are cited, because its 1.17 description still shows the old scaling.

heroes.pick_when: Pick short-window burst and a coordinated isolation target, rather than a generic attack-speed carry plan.
heroes.counterplay: Use his shot/reload rhythm to choose trades and avoid being the isolated low-health target. Keep allied area damage focused elsewhere if Reckoning removes the original focus.
heroes.reason: All cited text is unchanged on 1.17: the four-shot reload with a guaranteed final crit, the Obliterate missiles that prioritize Scar, and Reckoning pulling the target into the Nether Realm. The note agrees with the 2.32 plan, which buys no attack-speed items.

heroes.pick_when: Choose a confident ranged carry player with peel and a safe firing angle.
heroes.counterplay: Force flight or Hypercharge before the actual dive and use cover while the damage window runs. Flight changes the angle; it does not establish immunity to control or ranged pressure.
heroes.reason: RMB, E and R are unchanged on 1.17. Air Assault is a 3.75s hover with +100 range and no immunity; Hypercharge is a 5s fixed-rate window. The note is still true and agrees with the 2.32 plan.

heroes.pick_when: Pick sustained physical damage when allies can guarantee room to attack rather than just start a fight.
heroes.counterplay: Dive from a second angle after peel is spent or disengage from Inner Fire before returning. Never donate a stationary frontline target while she has a protected firing line.
heroes.reason: E, R and Passive are unchanged on 1.17. Relentless adds max-health damage per stack on basic attacks, which is why a stationary frontline target feeds her, and Inner Fire is a 3.5s barrage. The note is still true.

heroes.pick_when: Pick ability-attack weaving and self-repositioning for a practiced carry.
heroes.counterplay: Force Rocket Dash, then send the second threat. Keep moving through Ventilate's aim and avoid giving repeated free attack-spell exchanges while your escape is unavailable.
heroes.reason: The cited text is unchanged. The 1.17 hitbox change affects only the basic-attack projectile and is not described in the ability text, so the note stays accurate. Rocket Dash's cooldown falls when he damages heroes, which supports 'avoid giving repeated free attack-spell exchanges'.

counters.reason: Use Gag Grenade to deny a response after she becomes targetable, then preserve the airborne blast to separate.
counters.limit: Silence is short and the timing must follow the disappearance; damage still needs a safe firing line.
counters.review: Serath's 1.17 changes (basic-attack scaling, a lower Heresy burn) do not touch the tactic. Heaven's Fury still makes her vanish and then teleport to the marked target on the final strike, and Ascend is her follow-up response. Drongo's Gag Grenade silence (0.8-1.2s) and his airborne Shrapnel Cannon (launch away, brief CC immunity, push-back) are unchanged. Serath's R was dropped from the cited abilities because the tactic does not rely on Heresy. The Pred.gg carry table has no Drongo-versus-Serath row (she plays jungle).

counters.reason: Keep Gag Grenade to silence Narbash before he can start Crash Bang Boom!, and use a compatible anti-heal purchase if grouped restoration is the problem.
counters.limit: Silence alone is not sustained anti-heal, and the support can continue protecting after it ends. Whether silence ends a drum solo already in progress is not verified.
counters.review: Narbash's R text changed only in its per-hit scaling (4%/7% down to 3%/5%). Crash Bang Boom! is still a 3s channel. His grouped restoration still comes from Song of My People (Healing Aura) and March! (Healing). A compatible anti-heal purchase exists for Drongo: build adaptation #2, Tainted Rounds, which cuts healing by 45% on basic attacks. Drongo's E was dropped from the cited abilities because the tactic does not use Rad Rounds, and Narbash's Q was added for the March! healing. The Pred.gg carry table has no Drongo-versus-Narbash row. Uncertainty: neither 1.17 ability text states that silence interrupts an ongoing channel. This is retained prior advice, and the mechanic is unverified here. [2.34 consistency pass: aligned with the other role reviews and the 1.17 ability text.]

counters.reason: Attack the reachable frontline from protected range while Relentless stacks add max-health damage, and switch targets while Stone Forged Soul restores him.
counters.limit: Without peel, the ranged advantage disappears; Stoicism periodically deflects a basic attack, and a barrage spent into his Stasis heal is partly undone.
counters.review: The tactic holds on 1.17. Greystone lost base health (690 to 680) and armor growth (5.4 to 4.8), which makes him a slightly better attack target. Sparrow's Relentless adds 0.25% of max health per stack (up to 8) on basic attacks. The old limit called Stone Forged Soul an 'extra-life window'. The 1.17 text describes a 2.5s Stasis that restores 14/16/18% max health (more at low health), slows nearby enemies, then crashes down. There is no extra life, so the wording was corrected. The Stoicism passive deflects the next basic attack every 15s down to 4.8s by level, which matters specifically for an attack carry and is now named. Sparrow's E was dropped from the cited abilities. There is no Pred.gg Sparrow-versus-Greystone row (different roles).

adaptations.when: A reachable healing threat needs an answer before crit scaling
adaptations.reason: Buy compatible on-attack anti-heal earlier, then revisit the flexible finish. Do not make the swap when another ally already maintains the required debuff.
adaptations.review: Imperator is still the third core item of the 2.32 plan (Lightning Hawk > Vanquisher > Imperator). Tainted Rounds is a completed item with no 1.17 change. Its Blighted Strikes reduces the target's healing by 45% for 3s on basic attacks. It keeps 20% crit chance and adds 30% attack speed, but loses Imperator's 30% crit damage (Precision), which is the 'before crit scaling' trade-off the text describes.

adaptations.when: The fight rewards repeated Rad Rounds windows more than an execute
adaptations.reason: Rad Rounds now starts its cooldown on activation, making basic-attack cooldown support relevant. This is an uptime alternative with a burst tradeoff, not a promise of permanent irradiation.
adaptations.review: Vanquisher is still the second core item. Its Annihilate executes heroes below 5% health, which is the 'execute' named in the condition. The 1.17 Rad Rounds text still says 'The cooldown begins on activation'. Ashbringer has no 1.17 change: basic attacks cut current non-ultimate cooldowns by 8% (4% against non-heroes, 1.5x on crits), and it adds attack speed and 10 ability haste in place of Vanquisher's 12 penetration. The swap still makes sense.

adaptations.when: An enemy spell must be answered before a full damage commitment
adaptations.reason: Advance the existing spell shield only when it can absorb the relevant opener. Bait spells can remove it, and earlier defense delays the damage spike.
adaptations.review: The 2.32 plan is unchanged (Storm Breaker > Sky Splitter > Demolisher, then Imperator > Terminus > Mesmer). Imperator is the fourth item, and Mesmer is already the sixth, so this is a reorder (the engine flags it as one when the item is already in the plan). 'Advance the existing spell shield' describes exactly that. Mesmer has no 1.17 change: Vengeful Shroud blocks the next ability, on a 60s cooldown.

adaptations.when: Enemy shielding repeatedly prevents the physical ability conversion
adaptations.reason: Consider the current anti-shield item for the named shielding problem. It gives up Dread's magical armor and Vital Shield, so keep Dread when magical burst is the bigger threat; this is a flexible-slot answer, not an automatic response to any shield icon.
adaptations.review: Dread is still the sixth item of the 2.32 plan, whose why calls the finish defensive. Demon Edge has no 1.17 change. It has 50 physical power, 10 penetration, 200 health and 15 ability haste, and Demonic deals 45% bonus magical damage against shielded targets, capped at the shield's size. Penetration drops only slightly (12 to 10), so the rifle's per-penetration scaling and the ability build stay coherent; the old clause about keeping them coherent was dropped as vague. What the swap really costs is Dread's 40 magical armor and Vital Shield (it blocks 25% of magical damage from heroes). The old reason did not say so, and it now does.

notes_for_team_review: Murdock carry moves from C to B (the 1.17 buffs to Shots Fired, Buckshot and Long Arm of the Law, with 1.17 Gold+ results moving the same direction). No carry-pool change is recommended; the pool stays drongo, sparrow, legion, eden.

Legion is the carry-pool member with the weakest early 1.17 result (48.6% over 529 Gold+ against a 52.6% review sample). The grade and the pool slot were retained; recheck both when the sample grows. The compositions 'Grouped sustain and cleanup' and 'Prepared objective control' do not reference Press the Advantage, so the switch to Scorched Earth does not break them. Scorched Earth's napalm under the beam and mines actually fits their 'held route' and 'enemies remaining nearby' framing.

GRIM.exe carry was retained at B despite 40.2% over 127 Gold+ games (1.16.4 review 47.9% over 2142): there was no kit or patch reason, and the interval [32.0, 48.9] still contains the review rate. It is the first carry to recheck for C. The midlane GRIM.exe entry was not in my scope.

Composition 'Controlled front-to-back' (weakness) and the greystone hero note (counterplay) call Stone Forged Soul an 'extra life'. The 1.17 text describes a 2.5s Stasis heal with a proximity slow, then a crash, not an extra life. I corrected the same wording in counter #10; the offlane and composition reviewers should align theirs.

The Wraith carry and midlane tier entries previously shared why/watch text. I rewrote only the carry watch; the midlane reviewer should not assume the shared 'Carry has the better current role result' sentence still exists in the carry entry.

Typhoon (its Mirage dash cooldown rose from 35 to 45s, and its magical-power attack-speed scaling fell) appears in no carry plan, carry adaptation or assigned counter; it is also a component (completed_item false) in the Gold+ bundle. No carry text needs a Typhoon change.

Source-text lags to be aware of: Murdock's 1.17 Passive description still reads 36-60% although the official notes give 40-64%. Eden's Passive description was reworded with no official 1.17 note. Neither is cited numerically in my texts.

Counter #7 (Drongo into Narbash) was retained as prior advice, but neither ability text confirms that silence interrupts an ongoing channel. Do not build new composition advice on that interaction until it is verified.

tiers.why: Imperial Lash and Iron Rose give a protected catch; Crown of Thorns helps allies convert contact.
tiers.watch: Lower current role results temper the utility. Tyrant of Thorns removes Royal Flourish control, so the offlane damage plan is not the support peel plan.
tiers.reason: No official 1.17 change to Adele. The support plan (Dawnstar > Xenia > Dynamo, Seeds of Dominion) still uses Imperial Lash and Royal Flourish for the opening, so the why/watch text (Tyrant of Thorns is the offlane plan, not the support peel plan) remains accurate. 1.16.4 Gold+ review sample 46.9% over 3076; 1.17 Gold+ 48.1% over 243 [41.9, 54.4] includes the review rate. Bronze+ 47.2% over 483 is nested and points the same way.
tiers.limitation: 1.17 sample covers about 1.5 days; the interval is about +/-6 points.

tiers.why: Dread Nova gives a repeatable ranged catch and Ether Crystal changes where the fight happens; Particle Shredder converts the opening when it is safe to channel.
tiers.watch: Support income limits his damage engine, and his previous-patch Gold+ support results were well below midlane. Pick him only when the team already has a durable entry.
tiers.reason: Grade retained: no official 1.17 change to Argus. Text rewritten because the old why/watch was the shared midlane text and 'the much weaker support results' is a 1.16.4 fact; the new text follows the 2.32 support plan (Timewarp > Tainted Scepter > Dynamo, control windows on support income). 1.16.4 Gold+ review 44.0% over 1787; 1.17 Gold+ 47.9% over 146 [40.0, 56.0] includes the review rate. Bronze+ 49.6% over 466 is nested.
tiers.limitation: 146 games clears eligibility only; the interval spans 16 points. The midlane comparison is a previous-patch fact.

tiers.why: Glacial Charge and Hoarfrost give repeatable access and escape; Cryoseism can punish enemies gathering around an objective.
tiers.watch: Jungle is the priority on current role evidence. Do not transfer that grade to offlane or support, and keep an exit after the first control cycle.
tiers.reason: The 1.17 Shatter on-hit magical scaling cut (30% to 25%) affects basic-attack damage, not the support job, which the 2.32 support plan builds around Hoarfrost, Cryoseism and Glacial Thorns control. The why/watch remains accurate. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 48.0% over 1085; 1.17 Gold+ 50.7% over 73 [39.5, 61.8], below the 100-game threshold. Bronze+ 53.1% over 143 is nested.
tiers.limitation: 1.17 support sample is under 100 games; no grade movement can rest on it.

tiers.why: Control and projectile accuracy can still buy valuable attack time, but the dated Gold+ sample does not support default A priority. Choose for the needed fence and peel tools rather than treating kit fit as demonstrated pair success.
tiers.watch: This grade values control despite slightly negative role results. Missed skill shots and poor fence timing reduce the benefit substantially.
tiers.reason: No official 1.17 change to Dekker; Stasis Bomb, Containment Fence and Ion Strike text is unchanged and matches the 2.32 plan (control and safe positioning, no native heal or shield). 1.16.4 Gold+ review 47.7% over 6252; 1.17 Gold+ 49.0% over 486 [44.6, 53.4] includes the review rate. Bronze+ 48.3% over 1206 is nested and agrees.
tiers.limitation: 1.17 interval is about +/-4.5 points; the grade rests mainly on the previous-patch sample.

tiers.why: Sticky Mine pressures a position and Tesla Dome punishes enemies held in a choke; Security Gate provides an escape or peel route.
tiers.watch: Midlane supplies the farming economy. Support is a smaller-sample damage-utility option when the team already has frontline and reliable initiation.
tiers.reason: 1.17 raised empowered Sticky Mine damage and Security Gate's allied movement speed (40% to 50%) and raised the gate's mana cost (65 to 75). These are modest gains to pressure and repositioning, not a change of job; the why/watch remains accurate. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 50.3% over 791; 1.17 Gold+ 48.4% over 93 [38.5, 58.4], under 100 games. Bronze+ 50.5% over 188 is nested.
tiers.limitation: 1.17 support sample is under 100 games; the direction of the buffs is not yet visible in results.

tiers.why: Seismic Assault gives a compact catch into Void Bomb; Neural Disruptor adds a finishing threat that depends on the target's mana state.
tiers.watch: Midlane has the stronger role evidence. On a support budget Neural Disruptor carries less burst, so the grade rests on landing Seismic Assault for allies.
tiers.reason: Grade retained: no official 1.17 change to Lt. Belica. Watch rewritten because 'the attack-oriented augment requires a separate build interpretation' is stale; both 2.32 plans now use Combat Veteran, and the support plan centres on the Seismic Assault opening. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 50.3% over 2880; 1.17 Gold+ 49.6% over 244 [43.4, 55.8] includes the review rate. Bronze+ 47.4% over 663 is nested and lower.
tiers.limitation: A at a near-even rate is a utility judgement; the 1.17 interval is about +/-6 points.

tiers.why: Maco Gift! can sustain an ally around a chosen space, while Maco Strike! supplies control and Maco Fly! changes the supporting angle.
tiers.watch: His previous-patch Gold+ support sample was weak despite useful tools. Healing requires allies to stay in range, and spending Maco Fly! forward can leave him without an exit.
tiers.reason: Grade retained: no official 1.17 change to Maco. Watch rewritten because 'the current support sample is weak' described 1.16.4, and the 2.32 plan now says to preserve Maco Fly! when spending it leaves no safe exit. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 47.5% over 2319; 1.17 Gold+ 53.9% over 141 [45.7, 61.9] includes the review rate, with no kit reason for a raise. Bronze+ 48.5% over 291 is nested and does not agree with the Gold+ rise.
tiers.limitation: 141 games is eligibility only; a high early rate alone is not grounds to raise the grade.

tiers.why: Abduct creates a catch while Contagion supplies allied sustain; Beguile offers another response as the fight develops.
tiers.watch: Keep a defensive response after initiating. Eclipse connects distant pressure but should not be interpreted as relocating teammates.
tiers.reason: No official 1.17 change to Mourn. Eclipse's source text now says Mourn 'channels to absorb all light'; the effect, duration, Contagion and movement speed are unchanged, and the why/watch makes no claim that depends on the wording. The 2.32 plan (Hexbound Bracers > Dynamo > Astral Catalyst) still fits the catch-plus-sustain job; Hexbound's heal and shield power fell from 10% to 8%, which the tier text does not rely on. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 53.1% over 5743; 1.17 Gold+ 52.3% over 386 [47.4, 57.3] includes the review rate. Bronze+ 51.7% over 731 is nested.
tiers.limitation: Whether interrupting Mourn now ends Eclipse is not verified; the text wording alone does not establish it.

tiers.why: Consecrated Ground and Alacrity heal, shield and speed an attacking ally; Reversal Of Fortune can protect a committed teammate across the map.
tiers.watch: 1.17 trimmed her durability, passive amplification, Alacrity shield scaling and Reversal's damage reduction, and raised Reversal's cost; re-check the grade as 1.17 data grows. Choose her when the team supplies a way to begin fights.
tiers.reason: Grade retained, text updated. The kit reason for a lower grade is real: armour growth 5.5 to 5.1, regen 1.8 to 1.6, mana growth 55 to 52, Sentinel heal/shield power 12%-20.5% to 10%-16.8%, Alacrity shield scaling 60% to 50%, Reversal damage reduction 35% to 30% and mana cost 100 to 100/125/150. The Consecrated Ground fix removes an unintended extra 10%, so the tooltip numbers are unchanged. But the evidence does not point the same way: 1.16.4 Gold+ review 54.4% over 4296; 1.17 Gold+ 55.1% over 283 [49.3, 60.8] includes the review rate, and Bronze+ 55.2% over 504 (nested, not independent) agrees. The policy requires both a kit reason and consistent evidence, so S stays, with the nerfs named in watch. Old watch removed the stale 'default repeated-attack amplification plan' line; the Revenant/Legion item swap lives in build adaptation #4.
tiers.limitation: The nerfs are broad and could erode her margin once the 1.17 sample grows; the current interval is about +/-6 points and covers about 1.5 days. Her S had margin (the highest 1.16.4 Gold+ support rate of the S group), which is part of why one patch of trims does not yet justify A.

tiers.why: Song Of My People and March! reward a team that moves together; Thunk supplies a catch before Crash Bang Boom! layers pressure.
tiers.watch: Grouped sustain, March movement and a direct Thunk catch make him a priority for a team that actually stays in range. Hold the ultimate until interruption can be covered.
tiers.reason: No official 1.17 change to Narbash. Crash Bang Boom!'s source text now shows lower per-hit scaling (4% to 3% magical power, 7% to 5% physical power); the final hit, mesmerize and stun are unchanged, and the why/watch makes no numeric claim. The 2.32 plan (Truesilver Bracelet > Crystal Tear > Dynamo) still supports grouped sustain and protects the channel start. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 52.6% over 3617; 1.17 Gold+ 55.1% over 274 [49.2, 60.9] includes the review rate. Bronze+ 49.8% over 625 is lower; it is nested, so it is not an independent signal.
tiers.limitation: The per-hit scaling change is not in the official notes; it may be a text correction or an unannounced change.

tiers.why: Telekinetic Link and Hyperflux can amplify repeated attacks; Energy Lance and a timed pull can buy the linked ally space.
tiers.watch: 1.17 lowered her health, Essence Catalyst healing and Hyperflux attack speed, so trades are less safe and amplification is slightly smaller. This stays a partner-dependent grade; a premature pull can undo a good commitment.
tiers.reason: Grade retained, watch updated. Kit reason for a lower grade: health 670 to 660, Essence Catalyst healing 12-80 to 10-61, Hyperflux attack speed 40/60/80% to 35/55/75%. The evidence does not clearly move: 1.16.4 Gold+ review 50.3% over 4424; 1.17 Gold+ 49.7% over 346 [44.5, 55.0], a 0.6-point dip well inside the interval; Bronze+ 50.1% over 883 (nested) is flat. Her 1.17 hero-wide Gold+ bans are 1150, so opponents still treat her as a threat. Link and pull mechanics are unchanged.
tiers.limitation: A was already a generous grade for a near-even rate; if the 1.17 sample settles below the 1.16.4 rate, A to B would be the next step. Hyperflux movement speed text changed from 135% to 35% without an official note.

tiers.why: Riplash into Shock Therapy or Skewer creates a dangerous pick when allies are in range to follow.
tiers.watch: The grade depends on landing Riplash. Keep an exit and a second peel tool after a miss, and stay near allies who can convert the pull.
tiers.reason: Grade retained: no official 1.17 change to Riktor. Watch rewritten because the shared text cited 'current offlane results are particularly weak', a 1.16.4 cross-role fact. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 48.6% over 8327; 1.17 Gold+ 46.2% over 638 [42.4, 50.1] includes the review rate. Bronze+ 49.1% over 1183 is nested and higher. No kit reason supports C.
tiers.limitation: The 1.17 Gold+ point estimate is lower and the upper bound is near 50%; watch whether it holds as the sample grows.

tiers.why: Shield Bash and Shield Slam provide clear catch conversion, while Force Shield can protect an approach or the backline.
tiers.watch: Heavy Metal basic attacks no longer break spell shields on 1.17, so keep a separate answer for one before engaging. Catch value depends on allied damage close enough to convert Shield Slam.
tiers.reason: Grade retained: no official 1.17 kit change; Shield Bash, Force Shield and Shield Slam text is unchanged. Watch rewritten because the shared text discussed jungle and offlane samples, and the reviewed hero note records that Heavy Metal basics no longer remove spell shields (the support plan still uses Heavy Metal). 1.16.4 Gold+ review 51.6% over 8936; 1.17 Gold+ 51.5% over 748 [47.9, 55.0], essentially unchanged. Bronze+ 52.3% over 1523 is nested and agrees.
tiers.limitation: Spell-shield interaction comes from the official note and the reviewed hero context; which enemy items count as spell shields was not re-verified here.

tiers.why: Harvest Nettles supports repeated lane pressure; Fly Trap and Bramble Patch turn constrained movement into a clear follow-up opportunity.
tiers.watch: Midlane has the larger established sample. Support is a smaller-sample option needing frontline elsewhere, and the delayed ultimate still needs setup or a constrained path.
tiers.reason: No official 1.17 change to The Fey; Harvest Nettles, Bramble Patch and Fly Trap text is unchanged and matches the 2.32 support plan. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 52.8% over 817; 1.17 Gold+ 59.7% over 72 [48.2, 70.3], under 100 games, so it cannot support a raise. Bronze+ 56.1% over 171 is nested.
tiers.limitation: 1.17 support sample is under 100 games; a high early rate is not grounds for S.

tiers.why: Infuse heals a damaged ally, Ricochet can create a catch, and Neural Regenesis protects a planned fight.
tiers.watch: 1.17 raised Infuse's missing-health healing and shortened early Neural Regenesis cooldowns, but her previous-patch support results were below the leading enchanters. Do not treat the offlane damage plan as the support plan.
tiers.reason: Grade retained, text updated. 1.17 buffs: Infuse missing-health modifier 40% to 50%, Neural Regenesis cooldown 160/140/120 to 150/135/120, attack speed 110% to 115% with base attack time 1.4 to 1.5 (opposing, not a clean buff). These are modest and apply most to rank 1-2 of the ultimate. 1.16.4 Gold+ review 46.6% over 3484; 1.17 Gold+ 51.5% over 270 [45.5, 57.4] includes the review rate, so the interval does not exclude it. Bronze+ 49.6% over 734 is nested and weaker. A one-step raise would lean on a high early rate, which the standard does not allow.
tiers.limitation: If the 1.17 rise persists with a larger sample, B to A is plausible given the Infuse buff.

heroes.pick_when: Pick ranged catch and peel when another slot supplies the frontline.
heroes.counterplay: Move laterally around Stasis Bomb and keep movement for the fence. A containment boundary is not a silence; use the response your hero actually has instead of waiting inside it.
heroes.reason: No 1.17 change; Stasis Bomb, Containment Fence and Ion Strike text is identical. Pick and counterplay text still match the kit and the 2.32 plan. Dropped Passive from the cited keys because the text does not rely on Rocket Boots.

heroes.pick_when: Choose an ally-focused support when the team can stay in range of his chosen space.
heroes.counterplay: Separate the carry from the support zone, contest the movement landing and avoid stacking for Maco Strike. Anti-heal helps only if someone can keep it applied to the healing recipient.
heroes.reason: No 1.17 change; Maco Gift!, Maco Fly! and Maco Strike! text is identical and consistent with the 2.32 plan (alternate healing and damage, preserve Fly for an exit).

heroes.pick_when: Pick catch plus sustain when you want both a way in and a defensive response afterward.
heroes.counterplay: Use units and angles against the first-target Abduct line. Spread from close sustain pressure and regroup safely during Eclipse instead of chasing through the loss of vision.
heroes.reason: Abduct, Contagion and Beguile are unchanged. Eclipse's 1.17 source text now reads 'channels to absorb all light'; the reduced vision, Contagion spread and movement speed are the same, and the counterplay (regroup safely during Eclipse, do not chase through lost vision) remains true. The cited R text will update to the 1.17 wording.
heroes.limitation: The new 'channels' wording is not in the official notes; whether control on Mourn cancels Eclipse is unverified, so the note does not recommend interrupting it.

heroes.pick_when: Pair her amplification and protection with a reliable damage threat and initiation elsewhere.
heroes.counterplay: Force protection on one target before switching focus, and punish her forward positioning: 1.17 lowered her durability. Track Reversal's landing and Serenity's charged stun; anti-shield does not replace interrupting or escaping the allied damage hero she enables.
heroes.reason: pick_when still true. Alacrity (shield scaling 60% to 50%) and Reversal (damage reduction 35% to 30%, higher mana cost) changed text; the note makes no numeric claim about them. Added the 1.17 durability loss (armour growth, regen) to counterplay, matching the reviewed hero context that positioning matters more, and replaced the ambiguous 'aim' with Serenity's charged stun on arrival.
heroes.limitation: Whether lower armour growth and regen are enough to make her a priority target is a judgement, not a measured effect.

heroes.pick_when: Pick grouped sustain and a direct Thunk catch for an organized front-to-back fight.
heroes.counterplay: Spread or disengage from the prolonged group fight, apply anti-heal and keep a response for the ultimate channel. Bait Thunk before diving rather than treating his heal as his only threat.
heroes.reason: Thunk, Song of My People and March! are unchanged. Crash Bang Boom!'s per-hit scaling text is lower on 1.17 but the channel, slow stacks, mesmerize and final stun are the same; the counterplay (keep a response for the ultimate channel, bait Thunk) remains true. The cited R text will update.
heroes.limitation: The R scaling change is not in the official notes.

heroes.pick_when: Choose one dependable repeated-attack partner when the team already has initiation.
heroes.counterplay: Pressure the link positioning, separate the pair and wait out Hyperflux when possible. Bait the rescue pull before committing the second catch. Her lower 1.17 health and post-cast healing make early trades against her more rewarding; she does not supply a frontline.
heroes.reason: pick_when still true. 1.17 cut health, Essence Catalyst healing and Hyperflux attack speed; the reviewed hero context says she trades less safely. Counterplay now names that trade window, and cites Passive; dropped E because the text does not rely on Energy Lance.
heroes.limitation: Hyperflux movement speed text changed from 135% to 35% without an official note; the note makes no movement-speed claim.

counters.reason: Hold Shield Bash or Shield Slam for the reappearance/landing rather than spending both on the first tank.
counters.limit: The selected Crushing Descent adds a brief interrupt; do not assume she cannot interrupt your response.
counters.review: Steel's Shield Bash and Shield Slam are unchanged. Serath's Heaven's Fury still teleports to the marked target on the final strike and Ascend still lands a dive; the 2.32 jungle plan still selects Crushing Descent, so the limit stays accurate. Her 1.17 changes (attack scaling, Heresy burn) do not affect the timing.

counters.reason: Keep a hook or silence response for the channel rather than opening with every control tool. In melee range, Shock Therapy destroys shields before its damage and silence; time it before the 2.75-second transition.
counters.limit: A live Truesilver shield prevents control; break or wait out that protection before relying on the interrupt. Black Hole becomes non-cancellable after 2.75s of channeling, when Gideon may act. Protect or interrupt the early phase; after that point, prioritize positioning and leaving the zone.
counters.review: Riktor's Riplash and Shock Therapy are unchanged; Shock Therapy still destroys shields before its silence. Gideon's Black Hole still becomes non-cancellable after 2.75s; only its damage fell. Truesilver Bracelet's 1.17 effect still grants CC immunity while its shield holds, and Gideon's 2.32 plan still buys it, so the limit remains correct.

counters.reason: Reserve a reachable stun for Black Hole and avoid arriving alongside every allied damage hero.
counters.limit: Range and a shield that grants control immunity can prevent the intended interrupt. Black Hole becomes non-cancellable after 2.75s of channeling, when Gideon may act. Protect or interrupt the early phase; after that point, prioritize positioning and leaving the zone. A control hit does not bypass a still-active Truesilver shield.
counters.review: Steel's stuns are unchanged, Black Hole's 2.75s transition is unchanged, and Truesilver Bracelet still grants CC immunity while its shield holds. Heavy Metal no longer breaking spell shields does not affect this text, which already says control does not bypass a live Truesilver shield.

counters.reason: Threaten the exposed enchanter with a confirmed hook so she must spend protection defensively.
counters.limit: A missed hook is not pressure; allies must reach the catch before she or the carry can reverse it.
counters.review: Riktor's kit is unchanged. Muriel's Alacrity and Reversal texts changed (lower shield scaling, lower damage reduction, higher ultimate cost) and her armour growth and regen fell, which if anything makes a confirmed hook on her more threatening; the tactic and limit remain true. Pred.gg Gold+ shows Riktor 45% over 42 against Muriel, too small to weigh.

counters.reason: Use the stun and fence to break access after Ambush rather than fight his full sustained-contact window.
counters.limit: Invigorate cleanses the stun, and Ambush or allied follow-up can still reconnect; draw out the cleanse and watch the actual route.
counters.review: Dekker and Khaimera are unchanged on 1.17 and the tactic holds. The limit omitted Invigorate, which cleanses all debuffs and grants brief crowd-control immunity, so a stun spent before it can be undone. Dekker's Pred.gg Gold+ support table has no Khaimera row with 15 or more games, so there is no statistical signal either way.

counters.reason: Force the linked pair to split their attention with a catch angle and vision denial.
counters.limit: A saved pull can undo an unsupported catch; wait for the second opening rather than chasing both targets.
counters.review: Abduct is unchanged and Eclipse still reduces enemy vision for 4s (now worded as a channel). Phase's link and pull are unchanged; Hyperflux's attack speed fell, and her health and post-cast healing are lower, which slightly helps the catch. The limit remains accurate. Pred.gg Gold+ shows Mourn 35% over 20 against Phase: under 100 games, noted but not decisive.

counters.reason: Keep control beside the threatened carry and deny the exposed finishing route after Kallari reveals.
counters.limit: Force Shield is a projectile answer, not a universal defense against melee attacks.
counters.review: Steel's control and Force Shield are unchanged, and Kallari's Shadow Walk is still revealed by nearby enemy heroes and wards before Guillotine. Kallari had no 1.17 change. The limit remains accurate: Force Shield blocks projectiles, not her melee attacks or dash.

counters.reason: Threaten the short firing window with a direct catch and keep a separate response for the isolated ally's return.
counters.limit: Reckoning can remove your intended focus from allied damage; coordinate which target remains reachable.
counters.review: Steel is unchanged, and Revenant had no 1.17 change: the four-shot reload rhythm and Reckoning's isolation are the same, and the 2.32 carry plan still commits around the fourth shot. Tactic and limit remain true.

adaptations.when: The protected partner is a burst-oriented Revenant or ability Legion
adaptations.reason: Advance the existing healing/shielding-triggered item for Muriel’s own power and shared haste. Its power buff is magical: do not call it a physical-power amplifier for Revenant or Legion. Later Marshal still requires an ally who can use its attack speed and its local range.
adaptations.review: The 2.32 Muriel support plan (Marshal > Crystal Tear > Windcaller || Devotion > Vanguardian > Everbloom) still contains Marshal and Crystal Tear, so the row is a reorder that advances Crystal Tear, as its reason says. Crystal Tear's 1.17 Elation effect still gives both Muriel and the healed or shielded hero 30 Magical Power and 15 Ability Haste for 5s, so 'magical, not physical' and 'shared haste' remain correct. Marshal's Sheriff aura is still attack speed and on-hit magic damage for nearby heroes. Neither item changed on 1.17. Muriel's lower Sentinel and Alacrity values do not stop her heals and shields from triggering Elation.

notes_for_team_review: Muriel compositions ('Buy time for Sparrow', 'Protect the channel', 'Peel before damage', 'Compact catch with protection') rely on Reversal Of Fortune's protection: its damage reduction fell from 35% to 30% and its mana cost rose to 100/125/150. Check that no composition text quotes 35%.

Mourn's Eclipse is now worded as a channel in the 1.17 source text (not in the official notes). Compositions 'Second-wave dive' and 'Controlled front-to-back' should not claim it cannot be interrupted, nor that interrupting ends it; neither is verified.

Narbash's Crash Bang Boom! per-hit scaling is lower in the 1.17 source text (not in the official notes). Compositions 'Grouped sustain and cleanup' and 'Prepared objective control' should not quote drum-solo damage numbers.

Mourn's 2.32 support plan opens Hexbound Bracers, whose heal and shield power fell from 10% to 8%. The plan's stated reason (mana from damage taken) is unaffected; no support tier or hero note I reviewed relies on Transference.

Tier text is shared across roles for Steel, Riktor, Argus, Aurora, Adele, Gadget, Lt. Belica, The Fey and Zinx. I rewrote only the support entries. The jungle, offlane and midlane reviewers should check theirs; for example Steel's jungle/offlane watch and Riktor's jungle/offlane watch cite 1.16.4 cross-role samples.
Phase's Hyperflux movement speed text changed from 135% to 35% without an official note. Any pool or composition text that relies on a large Hyperflux movement burst should be checked.
Riktor support 1.17 Gold+ is 46.2% over 638 [42.4, 50.1]. It stays B, but it is the support grade most likely to fall if the 1.17 sample holds.

compositions.name: Containment into Black Hole
compositions.plan: Zarus identifies the reachable target before Coliseum; Gideon follows only after key interrupts are covered. Push the nearby wave before moving together to the objective entrance. Protect Gideon through the first 2.75s; then he can reposition while Black Hole finishes. A short catch does not guarantee the full channel.
compositions.weakness: The arena is not a stun. Escapes and a broken channel shield can defeat the follow-up, and on 1.17 a Ground effect such as Valmont's tether stops Torn Space, so plan Gideon's entry around it or have Zarus break the tether with control first.
compositions.review: Plan retained: Zarus's Coliseum (R) is unchanged on 1.17, and Gideon's Black Hole still becomes non-cancellable after 2.75s (only its damage fell to 500/760/1020), so the 2.75s line is still exact. Truesilver Bracelet, which the 2.32 Gideon plan still buys, grants control immunity only while its shield holds. Weakness changed: the official 1.17 bug fix prevents Torn Space (E) from teleporting when Gideon is hit by a Ground effect, and Gideon follows the catch with Torn Space. The only Ground source in the 1.17 kits is Valmont's tether (RMB, 'grounded and slowed'), which the kit says breaks if Valmont is affected by crowd control, so a Zarus Barricade stun is a verified answer. No claim is made about whether Truesilver's control immunity blocks Ground; that interaction is unverified.

compositions.name: Direct catch, compact burst
compositions.plan: Steel confirms Shield Bash or Shield Slam; Belica follows with Seismic Assault and Void Bomb without wasting both controls at once. Convert the pick into nearby vision or an objective.
compositions.weakness: Two control tools do not replace damage economy. Steel's early 1.17 jungle sample is very small, and his Heavy Metal attacks no longer break spell shields, so bring another answer before the stun.
compositions.review: Plan retained: Shield Bash (RMB, 0.5s stun) and Shield Slam (R, knock-up and 1.5s stun) are unchanged, as are Belica's Seismic Assault (Q) and Void Bomb (RMB); Belica had no 1.17 change. Weakness changed: 'the smaller current sample' was a 1.16.4 comparison; on 1.17 Steel jungle has only 62 Gold+ games (A retained by the jungle reviewer, below eligibility). The official 1.17 text says Heavy Metal basic attacks do not destroy spell shields, and the 2.32 Steel jungle plan runs Heavy Metal, so a catch that opens on a spell-shielded target needs a separate answer.

compositions.name: Second-wave dive
compositions.plan: Mourn creates the first catch while Serath waits for enemy peel, then enters the reachable target. Keep a response beside the allied carry instead of both chasing the reset.
compositions.weakness: No takedown means no visage extension. An early unsupported Serath entry defeats the plan.
compositions.review: Retained. Mourn's Abduct (RMB) still pulls the first enemy hit and slows it 90%, so 'Mourn creates the first catch' holds; Eclipse is not cited, so its new channel wording does not matter here. Serath moved S to A in jungle, but her second-wave job is unchanged: Heaven's Fury still vanishes and teleports on the final strike, the 2.32 plan's Crushing Descent gives Ascend its stun, and the Passive visage still grants a free Heresy and a 65% basic-cooldown cut only after a takedown, which is what 'no takedown means no visage extension' says. The text never calls her the top jungle priority.

compositions.name: Buy time for Sparrow
compositions.plan: Muriel times amplification and protection to a safe firing window; Sparrow attacks the nearest useful target. Other roles must provide the opening and a durable body.
compositions.weakness: This duo lacks dependable long-range initiation; it cannot solve a flank by damage alone.
compositions.review: Retained. Muriel's Consecrated Ground and Alacrity still grant attack speed, healing, a shield and movement speed, and the 2.32 plan opens Marshal for an attacking ally, so 'times amplification and protection to a safe firing window' holds after the 1.17 trims. No Reversal percentage is quoted. Sparrow had no 1.17 kit change; Heightened Senses is a stealth reposition, not a dash, so she still needs other roles for the opening and a durable body. Wind-Rider's cut (20% to 15%) is a small loadout trim.

compositions.name: Protect the channel
compositions.plan: Set the target with Zarus, reserve protection for Gideon’s entry and channel, and keep Reversal for a valid distant commitment. Leave a route back toward the carry. Protect Gideon through the first 2.75s; then he can reposition while Black Hole finishes. A short catch does not guarantee the full channel.
compositions.weakness: Spending all protection on the first entry exposes the next fight. Do not assume a shield survives burst or anti-shield: 1.17 lowered Reversal's damage reduction and raised its cost, and a Ground effect now stops Torn Space, so Muriel's protection cannot guarantee Gideon's entry.
compositions.review: Plan retained: it quotes no Reversal number, and 'keep Reversal for a valid distant commitment' still matches the 1.17 R text (target an allied hero anywhere, damage reduction plus a shield while Muriel flies in). The Gideon channel line is still exact. Weakness changed to state the two 1.17 facts the trio relies on: Reversal Of Fortune's damage reduction fell from 35% to 30% and its mana cost rose to 100/125/150 (official), and Torn Space no longer teleports when Gideon is hit by a Ground effect (official bug fix; Valmont's tether is the kit source). The percentages are not quoted in the displayed text.

compositions.name: Catch, silence, convert
compositions.plan: Layer a confirmed stun into Belica’s burst; Drongo uses silence to obstruct the response and keeps attacking within Rad Rounds. Plan the airborne blast direction before using it.
compositions.weakness: No sustain support is included yet. Reserve another role for protection and avoid displacing the focus out of allied damage.
compositions.review: Retained. Steel's stuns, Belica's Seismic Assault and Void Bomb, Drongo's Gag Grenade silence (0.8-1.2s), Rad Rounds window and Shrapnel Cannon's in-air launch and push-back are unchanged on 1.17. 'Obstruct the response' relies on silence preventing ability casts, not on silence ending a channel, so the unverified counter #7 interaction is not used. The push-back warning ('avoid displacing the focus') is still correct. The Heavy Metal spell-shield caveat is carried by Steel's jungle tier watch and composition 1 rather than repeated here.

compositions.name: Grouped sustain and cleanup
compositions.plan: Aurora controls the approach, Narbash follows with Thunk and grouped sustain, and Legion places physical area pressure on the held route. Move together before starting the objective.
compositions.weakness: The control is partly delayed. Anti-heal, dispersed targets or a second flank can break the grouped fight.
compositions.review: Retained. Aurora's only 1.17 change is basic-attack on-hit scaling; Hoarfrost, Glacial Charge and the 1.5s-delayed Cryoseism are unchanged, which is the 'partly delayed' control. Narbash's Thunk, Song of My People and March! are unchanged, and the plan quotes no drum-solo numbers, so the lower Crash Bang Boom! per-hit scaling in the 1.17 source text does not affect it. Legion stays S in carry; the 2.32 Scorched Earth plan leaves napalm where mines and the beam land, which fits 'area pressure on the held route'. His weak early 1.17 result is handled in the pool order and notes, not here.

compositions.name: Peel before damage
compositions.plan: Steel takes the first contact while retaining a control tool for the diver. Muriel keeps Sparrow firing; only commit the objective when the remaining roles can provide magical damage and wave control.
compositions.weakness: The trio alone has no dedicated magical damage plan and can overcommit its only initiating tank.
compositions.review: Retained. Steel's Shield Bash, Force Shield and Shield Slam are unchanged, so taking first contact while keeping a control tool for the diver still works, and Heavy Metal is not relied on for peel. Muriel's protection still keeps Sparrow firing after the 1.17 trims (no numbers quoted). The weakness is still accurate: none of the three is a dedicated magical damage plan.

compositions.name: Controlled front-to-back
compositions.plan: Greystone pressures space while Steel or Mourn confirms the catch. Gideon follows; Sparrow attacks from behind the second body. Keep one support control for the counter-dive and use the won space for objectives. Protect Gideon through the first 2.75s; then he can reposition while Black Hole finishes. A short catch does not guarantee the full channel.
compositions.weakness: Do not overlap every control or throw all three frontliners into the channel area. Greystone's Stone Forged Soul is a 2.5s stasis heal that slows nearby enemies, not an extra life and not peel for Sparrow; 1.17 also lowered his base health and armor growth.
compositions.review: Plan retained: Mourn's Abduct (RMB) and Steel's stuns still confirm the catch, the Gideon 2.75s line is exact, and Sparrow's plan still needs a second body in front. Weakness changed: it called Stone Forged Soul an 'extra life'. The 1.17 R text puts Greystone in Stasis for 2.5s, restores 14/16/18% max health (up to 2.5x at low health), slows nearby enemies by up to 70% by proximity, then crashes down; it is a heal window, not a second life. The carry reviewer corrected the same wording in counter #10. The official 1.17 base health (690 to 680) and armor growth (5.4 to 4.8) nerf is added because the plan uses Greystone as a frontliner; the offlane S grade was retained. Mourn's Eclipse is not mentioned, so its unverified channel wording does not affect this row.

compositions.name: Compact catch with protection
compositions.plan: Use Zarus or Belica to identify a single target, Drongo to constrain the response, and Muriel to protect the actual damage window. Akeron occupies the close entrance while the team keeps a ranged exit.
compositions.weakness: Akeron and Zarus can overcommit together. Disengage from failed catches rather than chase past Muriel and the carries.
