compositions.review: Retained. Zarus and Belica are unchanged catch tools; Drongo's silence and in-air blast are unchanged; Muriel still protects a damage window. Akeron's 1.17 change moved scaling from magic to health (Crushing Maw bonus-health scaling 4% to 4.5%), and the 2.32 offlane plan is health-built, so 'occupies the close entrance' with Web Lash and Crushing Maw still fits; his controls kept their effects. No Reversal number is quoted.

compositions.name: Prepared objective control
compositions.plan: Arrive first, establish vision and layer Aurora/Fey control over Legion’s physical area damage. Narbash supports the grouped advance while Greystone occupies the second angle.
compositions.weakness: Several effects require time and enemies remaining nearby. Do not force into spread ranged poke or ignore a flank while standing together.
compositions.review: Retained. Aurora's and The Fey's control (Hoarfrost root, delayed Cryoseism, Bramble Patch, delayed Fly Trap pull) are unchanged, matching 'several effects require time and enemies remaining nearby'. Legion's Scorched Earth napalm fits that framing. Narbash's grouped advance relies on Song of My People and March!, unchanged; no drum-solo numbers are quoted. Greystone 'occupies the second angle' makes no survival claim, so the durability nerf does not break it.

compositions.name: Protected second entry
compositions.plan: Akeron and Steel establish contact; Belica confirms a target. Serath waits for peel to be spent while Eden maintains a reachable firing pattern. Save one Steel control for the counter-dive.
compositions.weakness: Two mechanical damage picks make execution demanding. Do not send both into the first control rotation or assume a reset will repair a failed opening.
compositions.review: Retained. Akeron (health build, controls intact) and Steel support (Shield Bash, Shield Slam, Force Shield unchanged) establish contact; Belica is unchanged. Serath is now A, but her kit still rewards waiting for peel to be spent. Eden's 1.17 Passive text now states attack speed converts into physical power; 'maintains a reachable firing pattern' does not depend on the old fixed-rate wording. 'Save one Steel control for the counter-dive' needs no Heavy Metal interaction.

team.pools_review: Jungle (changed): Zarus and Aurora stay first as the two S junglers. Khaimera (A) is added third: no 1.17 kit change and the steadiest large jungle sample (1.16.4 review 51.9% over 9061; 1.17 Gold+ 51.6% over 728, 95% 48.0-55.3), and his sustained-pressure job is not otherwise covered by the pool; his jungle plan and active hero note exist. Serath moves behind Khaimera because the review moved her S to A (kit nerfs plus a 1.17 interval of 42.9-51.7 that excludes her 53.3% review rate); she stays in the pool as the second-wave diver, a distinct job. Steel stays for the direct tank catch (A retained, but only 62 Gold+ games on 1.17 and Heavy Metal no longer breaks spell shields). Rampage stays last: A was retained because nothing in his kit or plan changed, and his dip (46.8% over 237, interval 40.6-53.2 includes 51.5%) cannot remove him on sample alone; the jungle reviewer flags him for the next review. Carry (reordered): Legion moves from third to last. He keeps S, but his early 1.17 result is the weakest of the pool (48.6% over 529 against a 52.6% review sample, interval 44.4-52.8) and the carry reviewer named him the S carry most worth rechecking; Eden is flat (52.9% in both). No carry is added; Revenant (A) remains the burst alternative outside the pool. Midlane (unchanged): all three S grades and Argus A were retained with no kit change; Valmont has no reviewed tier, and Morigesh's new B does not reach the pool. Offlane (unchanged): Greystone keeps S after a modest durability nerf; Akeron, Grux and Shinbi keep A. Grux's Stampede Ground interrupt is noted in his tier text. Support (unchanged): all four keep S. Muriel took the broadest 1.17 trims but her grade was retained, and Riktor (B, possible fall) is not in the pool. Every pooled hero has that role's plan in guidance.builds, none experimental; no pool leads with a hero the review moved down.
team.pools_note: Ordered working pools for Gold+ planning on patch 1.17. Choose the job first: direct catch, secondary dive, sustained damage or protection. These are reviewed preferences, not measured ranks; where a 1.17 grade moved, the order follows it. Specialist and lower-priority heroes remain selectable.
notes: Jungle: Zarus (containment for a mid or support to convert) and Aurora (layered magical control) are the S starting points on 1.17. Serath moved to A: 1.17 trimmed her on-hit and Heresy burn scaling and the Wind-Rider attack speed her plan uses, so she is the second-wave diver rather than the first pick. Khaimera (A) has the steadiest large early 1.17 jungle sample for sustained pressure. Steel is the direct tank catch, with a very small early jungle sample and Heavy Metal attacks that no longer break spell shields. Rampage stays A as a durable long-range boulder catch, but his early 1.17 dip is flagged for the next review.

Mid: Lt. Belica (compact catch), Gideon and The Fey (prepared area control) stay S. 1.17 trimmed Gideon's damage, and a Ground effect such as Valmont's tether now stops Torn Space, so protect his entry and channel rather than relying on raw damage. Argus, Gadget and Howitzer are A alternatives; Morigesh rose to B on her Hive and Curse buffs. Valmont is new on 1.17 and has no reviewed tier yet; his early Gold+ midlane sample (354 games, heavily banned) is too new to grade.

Carry: Drongo, Sparrow, Eden and Legion stay S. Drongo supplies silence and physical shred, Sparrow needs protected attack time, Eden rewards practiced heat and stance management, and Legion's Scorched Earth plan adds area pressure, though his early 1.17 result is the weakest of the four and should be rechecked. Revenant is the A burst alternative; Murdock rose to B on 1.17 damage buffs, and GRIM.exe's early drop has no kit reason yet.

Support: choose Steel for a direct opening, Mourn for catch plus sustain, Muriel for amplification and protection when initiation already exists, or Narbash for a grouped fight. Muriel keeps S after broad 1.17 trims, including a weaker and costlier Reversal, so position her carefully. Phase stays A after health and Hyperflux trims. Riktor remains a B hook-execution option, and his early 1.17 result makes him the support grade most likely to fall.

Offlane: Greystone remains the pressure default, but 1.17 lowered his base health and armor growth, and Stone Forged Soul is a 2.5s stasis heal, not an extra life. Akeron supplies sustain and frontline on a health build; Grux punishes reachable melee fights, though a Ground effect now interrupts Stampede; Shinbi supplies magical skirmishing. Scarlett and Iggy & Scorch are strong alternatives, Iggy only when another role supplies frontline. Countess's early offlane result fell despite the Feast fix. Terra and Serath offlane stay C and do not inherit another role's grade.

Pred.gg 1.17 matchup rows cover about 1.5 days and pool all roles, and the counter, anti-counter and lane-counter views are one table, not separate evidence. They describe observed games with the named hero present, not proof of a lane or ability interaction. Use the reviewed counterplay to decide which response you can execute.

Community builds are alternative hypotheses. The 2.32 build review compared their item sequences with 1.17 item effects and your role plan; popularity or a high conditional build rate cannot establish that a purchase caused the wins.

Patch 1.17 strategy review (23-24 September 2026) is a one-time pass, not a recurring schedule. Tier grades, hero notes, counter picks, build adaptations, compositions and pools were re-checked against exact 1.17 ability text, the official 1.17 notes and the 2.32 plans. Grades moved only where a kit or patch reason and the evidence pointed the same way: Serath jungle S to A, Countess jungle C to B, Morigesh midlane C to B and Murdock carry C to B.
team.notes_review: All eight notes rewritten for 1.17. Notes 0-4 named 1.16.4 facts ('Serath is the second-wave damage pick' under an S grade, 'Steel ... smaller current sample', 'Rampage remains a durable alternative rather than disappearing after nerfs', 'stronger current role evidence', 'Skylar and Revenant remain usable ... old automatic carry pool'). They now follow the five ledgers' grades: the four grade moves are named, Khaimera and the flagged Rampage, Legion and Riktor are described as the reviewers asked, and the 1.17 mechanics that change play are stated without numbers (Serath's scaling and Wind-Rider cuts, Heavy Metal and spell shields, Ground stopping Torn Space and interrupting Stampede, Muriel's Reversal trim, Phase's health and Hyperflux trim, Stone Forged Soul as a stasis heal). Hyperflux movement speed and Narbash's drum-solo scaling are not mentioned because their source-text changes are unannounced. Valmont's tether is named as the Ground source because it is the only one in the 1.17 kit text; the Vein Splitter exception is left to his plan. Note 5 now says the Pred.gg tables are one pooled table over about 1.5 days, per the brief. Note 6 now points at the 2.32 build review's 1.17 item comparison. Note 7 replaced the 14 September/20 September scheduling text with what this review is, and states it schedules nothing further, consistent with STRATEGY-REVIEW-POLICY.md's one-time-trial decision.

build_advice.name: Protect the first decisive channel
build_advice.text: Gideon's midlane plan buys Truesilver Bracelet as its protected-channel default, trading early flat penetration for survival of the Black Hole channel; Narbash opens with it to protect the start of Crash Bang Boom!. The bracelet grants control immunity only while its shield holds, and damage or anti-shield can remove that protection. Against little interrupt pressure, Gideon can buy Wraith Leggings earlier.
build_advice.review: Mechanics retained: Truesilver Bracelet has no 1.17 change (Reprisal: on casting your ultimate, a 100 (+18% health) shield for 4s, CC immune while it holds, explodes when removed), and Wraith Leggings is unchanged. The old text never named a hero, although only Gideon's plan has the Wraith Leggings reorder (adaptation #0) and Narbash's plan also opens Truesilver, so the heroes are now named. No claim is added about Truesilver versus Ground, which is unverified.

build_advice.name: Separate clear from catch utility
build_advice.text: Dynamo pays off only when you immobilize an enemy and allies hit it during the next 2.5s. The Riktor, Steel and Terra jungle plans pair Fire Blossom's burn clear with Dynamo for the catch; Overlord is the farming and health-stacking opener for plans where you are not the sole initiator, such as Greystone, Khaimera and Rampage. Do not buy both clear openers by habit while the next objective needs armor and catch utility.
build_advice.review: Neither item changed on 1.17. Dynamo's Immobilizer makes an immobilized enemy take 8% more damage for 2.5s; Overlord's Colossal Cleave scales with health and Devourer permanently adds health on kills. No 2.32 plan buys both Dynamo and Overlord, so the old 'do not buy both clear engines' was unclear about which two items it meant; the 2.32 tank junglers (Steel, Riktor, Terra) run Fire Blossom with Dynamo, while Greystone, Khaimera and Rampage open Overlord. Text rewritten to name that split; the advice itself is unchanged.

build_advice.name: Serath: finishing chain versus a marked duel
build_advice.text: Weald is the default Eternal for Serath's attack-speed and on-hit jungle plan. The 2.32 build review switched it from Thraex to Weald because Weald led in the 1.16 loadout samples; those are separate conditional samples, not a causal test, and 1.17 has not re-measured the split. Dryad's Boon still shortens basic-ability cooldowns on each attack, and Wind-Rider, which follows her teleport or leap entry, gives less attack speed on 1.17. Weald fires only against a hero below 30% health, with a 10s cooldown per hero, so it does not amplify every attack. Keep Thraex for a deliberately sustained marked-target duel.
build_advice.review: 'Current Pred.gg Jungle observations favor it' was stale: the 2.32 build review's basis was the 1.16 Statz loadout comparison (Weald ahead of Thraex in all four large brackets), and it states no Gold+ 1.17 loadout outcome exists. The 1.17 perk text confirms Weald (below 30% health, 10s per-hero cooldown), Dryad's Boon (0.15s basic-cooldown cut on hit) and Wind-Rider (now 15% attack speed after a dash, leap, teleport or leaving stealth; official cut from 20%). Serath's Heaven's Fury teleport and Ascend leap both trigger Wind-Rider. The jungle reviewer's S to A move does not change which loadout the plan uses.

build_advice.name: Carry buffs must fit the firing pattern
build_advice.text: Marshal fits repeated basic attacks. Revenant’s burst and Legion’s attack-speed conversion require their own item interpretation; do not buy a generic support aura simply because the ally occupies Carry.
build_advice.review: Marshal is unchanged on 1.17 (Sheriff: 15% attack speed and on-hit magical damage for nearby heroes), so it fits repeated basic attacks. Legion's 1.17 Passive still converts bonus attack speed into ability haste, and Revenant's plan buys no attack-speed item, so both still need their own interpretation. Consistent with support adaptation #4 (advance Crystal Tear for a Revenant or ability Legion partner), which the support reviewer retained.

team.summary: One-time Patch 1.17 strategy review for Gold+ play. Tier grades, hero counterplay, counter picks, build adaptations, compositions and working pools were re-checked against exact 1.17 ability text, the official 1.17 changes and the 2.32 build plans. Early 1.17 results cover about 1.5 days, so grades moved only where a kit reason and the evidence agreed. The playbook still favors a coherent win condition over assembling five high win rates.
team.title: Patch 1.17 decision playbook
team.historical_note: One-time review for patch 1.17, written on 23-24 September 2026 as a Gold+ (ranks 27-36) reference. Grades are dated editorial judgments, not win probabilities. Evidence limits: Pred.gg 1.17 Gold+ data covered about 1.5 days (fewer than 30 to about 770 games per hero and role, with intervals of roughly 4 to 18 points either way); Bronze+ figures contain the Gold+ games; the 14 September 1.16.4 review samples are large but from the previous patch; Statz is a lagging 1.16 comparison. Earlier council judgments and the 14 September review remain background, and observed rates, calculated kit fit and personal working pools stay separate.

consistency_findings.problem: HIGH. Contradicts the 1.17 R text and the other ledgers. The note was 'checked and retained' but still says 'Avoid spending every major cooldown into his extra life'. Stone Forged Soul is a 2.5s Stasis that heals 14/16/18% max health (more at low health), slows nearby enemies by proximity, then crashes down; it is not an extra life. The carry reviewer corrected the same wording in counter #10, and this team review corrects composition 8. The offlane reviewer's own reason describes the stasis correctly. Set verdict to 'changed'; keys Q, E, R still fit (add Passive only if Stoicism is mentioned).
consistency_findings.fix: Kite the 2.5s Stone Forged Soul stasis, which heals him and slows anyone close, then switch pressure when the ultimate commits and return after the crash. Avoid spending every major cooldown into that heal window while his carries attack freely.

consistency_findings.problem: MEDIUM. Kit attribution error that the midlane reviewer corrected only in the midlane entry. 'Knock, Knock! and Back It Up! create a repeated skill-shot window' credits Back It Up! (R, a delayed teleport of the target back to its position 2s earlier) with the repeat. The repeat comes from Peekaboo! (Q) marking targets: Knock, Knock! (RMB) that damages a marked unit refunds 35% mana and cuts its cooldown by 75%. Keys RMB, Q, R already cover the fix.
consistency_findings.fix: Peekaboo! marks a target so Knock, Knock! fires again sooner, with ranged attacks between casts; Back It Up! returns a target to where the team can follow.

consistency_findings.problem: MEDIUM. Sentence corrected in two ledgers but left in the jungle entry ('checked and retained'). 'Current offlane results are particularly weak' is a 1.16.4 cross-role fact; on 1.17 Gold+ offlane is 50.6% over 162, and the offlane and support reviewers both removed it from their shared Riktor text.
consistency_findings.fix: The grade depends on landing the hook. Keep an exit and preserve peel after a miss; his support catch is a separate job, and its grade does not transfer to jungle.

consistency_findings.problem: MEDIUM. Sentence corrected in jungle but left in offlane ('checked and retained'). 'Not an automatic promotion from favorable patch direction' refers to an earlier patch's buffs; the jungle reviewer called it stale and replaced it. Kwang's only 1.17 change is the Grounded sword-pickup bug fix.
consistency_findings.fix: Both dated role samples were below even and early 1.17 results are too, so treat him as a practiced sword-placement option for controlled fights. The Grounded sword-pickup fix is a reliability change, not a reason to promote him.

consistency_findings.problem: LOW-MEDIUM. Shared jungle text contradicts the offlane tier. The B offlane entry says 'The stronger jungle result and easy-to-coordinate containment support this priority', which describes the jungle S grade. Offlane is weaker in both samples (1.16.4 48.5% over 2510; 1.17 Gold+ 47.8% over 180) and the jungle entry keeps the original sentence correctly.
consistency_findings.fix: Jungle is his priority role; offlane is weaker in both the dated and the early 1.17 samples. Coliseum still needs an ally close enough to exploit it.

consistency_findings.problem: LOW-MEDIUM. Tier text now contradicts the jungle grade change. 'The strong jungle sample does not transfer' reads as current, but the jungle reviewer moved Serath jungle S to A because 1.17 cut her on-hit and Heresy scaling and her 1.17 jungle interval (42.9-51.7) excludes the 53.3% review rate. The same scaling cuts apply to her offlane damage.
consistency_findings.fix: The dated jungle result does not transfer to her small, weak offlane sample, and 1.17 trimmed the attack-uptime damage both roles use. Enter after key enemy control is spent rather than leading into every interrupt.

consistency_findings.problem: MEDIUM. Counter #7 (Drongo into Narbash) was retained, but 'Keep silence for the channel' relies on silence interrupting Crash Bang Boom! once it has started. The carry reviewer notes that neither 1.17 ability text states this, and the brief says an unverified mechanic may not support advice. Silence preventing a cast is not in doubt, so reword to that. Limit can stay, with one added clause.
consistency_findings.fix: reason: "Keep Gag Grenade to silence Narbash before he can start Crash Bang Boom!, and use a compatible anti-heal purchase if grouped restoration is the problem." limit: "Silence alone is not sustained anti-heal, and the support can continue protecting after it ends. Whether silence ends a drum solo already in progress is not verified."

consistency_findings.problem: LOW. Cross-role inconsistency, not a contradiction. The jungle reviewer rewrote Countess's shared why to describe the 1.17 Feast (bonus damage and full heal against Haemorrhaged targets); offlane and midlane still say 'Feast supplies a targeted conversion when the opponent cannot interrupt it'. The 1.17 R text says Feast suppresses the target for 0.75s before its damage and states nothing about Countess being interruptible, so the clause is unverified. Offlane keys already include Passive.
consistency_findings.fix: Shadow Slip and Blade Siphon support short trades; Feast converts a target after two ability hits apply Haemorrhage.

consistency_findings.problem: LOW. Same as the offlane Countess why: unverified 'cannot interrupt it' clause, and it differs from the jungle rewrite. If adopted, add Passive to ability_keys (currently RMB, Q, R) because the text would rely on Haemorrhage.
consistency_findings.fix: Shadow Slip and Blade Siphon support short trades; Feast converts a target after two ability hits apply Haemorrhage.

entries.reason: enrich_bundle stores this list as bundle.unverified_changes whenever live == packet patch, in place of all official changes (no page reads it today; exports and the shared server carry it). It now lists the 123 official 1.17/1.16.4 changes that no reviewed source field confirms (53 from 1.17, 70 from 1.16.4): base statistics, bugfix/QoL notes, and values the source does not state. The 52 old 1.16.4 rows were not carried over wholesale: rows the 1.17 source now states (e.g. L.I.N.X 48/69/90/111/132, Voracity +2 gold) drop out.

Eden generates Heat from dealing damage to Heroes. Upon reaching 300 Heat, Eden Overheats, gaining access to her Limit Break abilities. Heat will decay when not dealing damage to Heroes for 3.5s.
Heat Generation is increased by 12.5%/30%/47.5%/65% based on Ultimate Level.
Eden attacks at a fixed rate. Every 1% Bonus Attack Speed converts into 0.6 additional Physical Power.

khaimera.Passive:
Damaging Enemy Heroes or Jungle Monsters grants Khaimera Rage. Khaimera gains 0.1–1.54(+0.3% magical power) Health Regeneration (based on Level) and his Cooldowns progress 0.5% faster per 1 Rage.
While above 50 Rage, Khaimera gains 8% Movement Speed.
Rage decays at a rate of 25 per second after not attacking for 2.5s.

murdock.Passive: Landing 5 successful Basic Attacks will cause Murdock's next Basic Attack to have 400 increased range and deal (+40-64% physical power) bonus damage.

integration.why: abilities-1.17.json is the uncorrected Pred.gg 1.17 text. After this ledger (with patch-1.17.mech.json installed) these abilities show the reviewed text, so any strategy/tier/counter/composition row that cites them must copy the new text: eden and khaimera Passive (retained reconciliation of a malformed feed) and murdock Passive (official 1.17 scaling, both feeds stale). With the repository patch-1.17.json only the eden and khaimera changes apply.
integration.plans: Plan preconditions are not edited. Eleven exact build_patch_review.source_reconciliation entries (section build_patch_review.source_reconciliation) keep every plan that is active today active (90 of 97 in the dry run, both patch-1.17 files).
integration.install_patch117: patch-1.17.mech.json = apply_patch117(HEAD patch-1.17.json). apply_strategy.py does not write patch-1.17.json; install it with the packet, or the served site keeps the stale 1.16 text for the 28 fields listed under "patch-1.17 corrections".
integration.validator_patch_fields: mech_apply sets patch 1.17 only on mechanics rows. The validator also requires guidance.strategic_review.patch and guidance.meta_review.patch to equal the packet patch; those belong to the strategy integrator (probe-packet/apply_strategy set them). new_plans.title: 2.34 new build plans (Legion Midlane, Zinx Carry, Rampage Offlane) for live 1.17
new_plans.method: Kit first: each plan is reasoned from the exact 1.17 ability and item text and the hero's reviewed main-role plan, following observed purchases where they exist. Win rates are quoted as context only; none supports a choice.

legion|midlane.reasoning: Newly authored from the 1.17 kit. Mines, grenade and orbital all scale with physical power, the rifle and Orbital Sanction's radius bonus reward 30 penetration, and bonus attack speed converts to haste, so mid Legion is a physical area caster. The plan follows what mid players actually buy. The Pred.gg 1.17 Bronze+ Midlane item tables (108 games in their own base; the role row counts 83, which include the 31 Gold+ games) open with Malady in 70 games; the most common three-item core is Malady > Deathstalker > Spear Of Desolation (10 games); The Perforator (18 games third, 10 fifth) and Infernum (11 second, 11 fourth) are the common later purchases; and Scorched Earth (67 games), Ortus (61), Tithe of Death (17) and Mind Rot (23) lead their slots. The only Statz variant, 1.16 Bronze+ (471 games, Scorched Earth + Vesh, 49.7%), is the same core with The Perforator fourth. One departure from observed purchases: Vanquisher is the most common second item (28 games), but its critical chance helps only basic attacks and adds no haste, so the plan keeps Deathstalker, whose attack speed the passive turns into haste. Vesh is kept over Weald (27 and 28 games) because most mid Legion damage is ability damage and 1.17 reduced Weald's Forage and Wind-Rider.
legion|midlane.alternative: Vanquisher second (the most common Bronze+ second item, 28 games) with Press the Advantage (27 games) and the carry plan's Thraex (Savage Strikes + Rallying Roar), for a rifle-and-execute game. Not the default because critical chance adds nothing to the mines, grenade or orbital.
legion|midlane.limitation: Newly authored on very small samples: Pred.gg 1.17 Gold+ Midlane 31 games (22 wins) and Bronze+ 83 games (43 wins), which are nested, not independent. There is no Gold+ item or loadout sample; purchase counts are Bronze+ only and overlap between positions. No whole-build win rate is inferred.

pred_bronze_plus_1_17_positions.note: Position and loadout rows overlap and are never summed; the item tables cover 108 games in their own base, the role row 83. Counts show what is bought, not item strength.

zinx|carry.reasoning: Newly authored from the 1.17 kit. Refibrillator carries a physical base and a stacking magical damage-over-time effect scaled by magical power and level, so carry Zinx is an on-hit attacker with magical scaling, not a health-scaling bruiser or a healer: attack speed multiplies both parts, Prophecy adds magical on-hit damage, and Orion and Typhoon turn haste and attacking into more attack speed. Terminal Treatment is the only augment that raises on-hit damage (official 1.17: 35% to 25%); Disc Of Demise adds control, not attack damage. Weald, Prophecy > Spectra > Orion and Typhoon follow the only observed carry build (Statz 1.16 Diamond+, 89 games, Terminal Treatment + Weald, 58.4%); Weald's volley at heroes below 30% health applies on-hit effects at 30% effectiveness and gains projectiles from bonus attack speed. Of its blessings, Dryad's Boon lets attacks shorten Ricochet and Bad Medicine; Barkskin (41 games) is kept over Taproot (38), which heals from bonus physical power she does not buy, and Wind-Rider (10), which needs a dash. The finish (Magnify, Caustica, Spellbreaker) comes from the reviewed Zinx Offlane plan: sustain, magical penetration and spell protection. The 2.32 Offlane review noted weak 1.17 Bronze+ Offlane results for Orion and Spectra; those are another role's small item samples and are not treated as carry evidence.
zinx|carry.alternative: Disc Of Demise with Thraex (Savage Strikes + Ferocity) and the Offlane plan's Prophecy > Magnify > World Breaker opening: a sturdier spell-and-attack hybrid that relies on Ricochet control instead of the reduced Terminal Treatment.
zinx|carry.limitation: Newly authored on very small samples: Pred.gg 1.17 Gold+ Carry 23 games (12 wins) and Bronze+ 67 games (34 wins), which are nested, not independent. There is no Gold+ (or Bronze+) item or loadout sample; the only build observation is Statz 1.16 Diamond+ (89 games, previous patch). No whole-build win rate is inferred. The published Terminal Treatment text (Infuse, up to 60%) disagrees with the official note and current Pred.gg text (Refibrillator, up to 25%); the plan relies only on the official value.

rampage|offlane.reasoning: Newly authored from the 1.17 kit as a lane bruiser, not a jungle clear. Pounce, Rumble's passive physical power, Rumble's slow, Behemoth and the passive all scale with maximum health, so Krix and every item add health. The jungle plan's Predator (camp-leader kills) and the passive's doubled jungle regeneration do not apply in lane, so Cannibalism replaces Predator and Regenerative Tissue carries lane sustain. Elafrost gives armour, mana regeneration for 80-mana Pounce and Boulder Throw, and an empowered, slowing attack after each cast; Overlord keeps the jungle plan's health-scaling cleave for trades and waves, and its unit-kill health works on minions. Tainted Guard answers basic-attacking offlaners and opened the only observed offlane build (Statz 1.16 Paragon+, 10 games, The Rumbling + Nihil, 3 wins). Rock & Awe, Krix and Saphir's Mantle are kept from the reviewed jungle plan; Saphir's Mantle evolves from damage taken and unit kills, both of which happen in lane. Skills: Rumble first (its damage and health-to-power ratio rise and its cooldown falls from 9 to 5 seconds with rank), then Boulder Throw, whose base damage and stun rise with rank and whose damage Rock & Awe multiplies, as in the observed Paragon+ order.
rampage|offlane.alternative: The Rumbling with Nihil (Mana Siphon + Terror) and Tainted Guard > Syonic Echo > Elafrost, the only observed offlane build: constant Rumble for a lane that must hold waves, at the cost of a 60% self-slow while active and extra mana. Not the default: the sample is 10 games and the sources disagree on the augment (no cooldown in the published Paragon text, a refund on damage in current Pred.gg text).
rampage|offlane.limitation: Newly authored on very small samples: Pred.gg 1.17 Gold+ Offlane 18 games (10 wins) and Bronze+ 26 games (15 wins), which are nested, not independent. There is no Gold+ (or Bronze+) item or loadout sample; the only build observation is 10 Statz 1.16 Paragon+ games. No whole-build win rate is inferred.
